Industry observers note that after a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

According to recent reports, brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Industry observers note that kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick said. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick mentioned. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a substantial game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

In a recent development, at the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

In a recent development, SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge.

Mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf.

And after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

Pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060.

The turnaround was completed a few minutes later when De Cuyper found the net, finishing off a counter-attack in which Diego Gómez and Kostoulas raided the left flank of United before cutting the ball back.

Brighton have turned it around!!! 🔵A sensational comeback as Maxim De Cuyper makes it 3-2 at Old Trafford. pic.twitter.com/Bfcr4N7mTL.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

“We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler said. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”.

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”.

"We can't accept that" ❌"I take responsibility for that" 🗣️ Michael Carrick reacts to his side's defeat👇 pic.twitter.com/OheT8yUK7y.

I think we’ve got to be a little bit careful on that one. He’s a 15-year-old boy. It’s more about the welfare and the care of JJ as a child really, or certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we’ve got to be a little bit careful of the exposure and how we jump on that.

The start of the game and the end of the game was completely different, didn’t feel like the same game or the same emotions at all. We had the game exactly where we wanted it and let it get away from us in a big way.

There’s a number of things we’ll look at, we’ll dissect and I know quite a bit of where it went wrong. We can’t accept that as a group. I take responsibility, the performance towards the second half that’s on me. We’ll have to get better, we have a major game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to get back to winning football matches.

We’ve got to keep evolving as a group. We have to keep learning and dealing with situations. Sometimes they come a bit easier than others. Tonight was a tough one. We didn’t find a way out of it. That’s up to me and the staff to help the players and guide them through it. I think we all know that in the end tonight feels like a significant disappointment.

We’ve had small, little things that have gone against us in the last week or two and then it accumulates to feel that it’s a lot bigger. I think we have to be honest and say that. The late goal against Everton from outside the box. The [Manchester] City goal the other day. It can all of a sudden roll into something a bit greater but I understand the disappointment because we shouldn’t finish the game in that manner with the position we were in and we have to be humble and take that.

We have to find the answers for Sunday.

For the first time in 50 years, they lose a game at Old Trafford after leading 2-0. Another proud record falls in the post-Ferguson era.

The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the new season.

AC Milan have been linked with a move for Alejandro Balde, but Fabrizio Romano claims some flexibility is needed from Barcelona.

In the past couple of weeks there has been more talk about Milan strengthening in the left-back role. Pervis Estupinan has not been convincing since his arrival, while Davide Bartesaghi and Diego Moreira have been used further forward in recent weeks.

Yunus Musah was even adapted to playing as a left-sided defender in the recent win over Genoa, so it’s clear that Ruben Amorim might welcome a more natural player for the role, one that fits his ideas of how to play.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano touched upon a number of different topics connected to Milan, from Francesco Camarda’s fate to the possibility of a young midfielder arriving. He also spoke about Balde – another recent link – and his words are via MilanNews.

“Balde is a name that can be a key player in January. Then, to be completely honest, he’s a foreign transfer name, being realistic. He earns more than €5 million net per season,” he began.

“Balde still isn’t playing and will speak with Mendes today, who is on a mission to Barcelona to meet with the player and his family and figure out what to do in the January transfer window.

“I’d keep an eye on the possibility if the formula were to change, because these are at the moment foreign figures. But he’s a player to keep an eye on. We’ll see if he goes to Italy or abroad.”.

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 21:07.

Two of Ligue 1's form sides meet at Allianz Riviera this weekend as Nice seek to end Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak in Saturday's matchday-11 tussle.

Luis Enrique's men are chasing an eighth consecutive league victory and a 12th straight win across all competitions, while the Eaglets aim to build on a run that yielded nine points from nine before the hiatus.

Something has shifted for Olivier Pantaloni's men since they failed to defeat 10-man Lyon last month, with Les Aiglons embarking on their longest Ligue 1 winning streak of 2026.

Indeed, Nice have not won as many consecutive matches since October 2025, a sequence that proved the highlight for supporters during a campaign in which interim boss Claude Puel eventually steered Le Gym to safety following a 16th-placed finish.

Pantaloni's impressive start has helped the Eaglets put the 2025-26 campaign behind them, with five victories and two draws from their opening 10 matches leaving them sixth in the standings.

All five of Les Aiglons' victories have come in their last six games, underlining their improvement in performances and results after a four-match winless start that produced two draws.

Only PSG have collected more than Nice's 15 points across the last six gameweeks, but Pantaloni's team now seek to halt the capital club's remarkable winning run.

The Parisians failed to win any of their opening three matches of the 2026-27 season, losing once and drawing twice, but the reigning French and European champions have since turned the screw to lead the table.

Lille and Paris FC remain two and three points behind Enrique's men respectively, underlining how well those early-season high-flyers have kept pace with PSG's surge.

Enrique's side now travel to Allianz Riviera aiming to end the hosts' unbeaten home run, with Nice having collected 11 points from a possible 15 in front of their supporters.

Only Lyon, Paris and Rennes have earned more home points this season, with 13 apiece, underlining the significance of PSG's visit on Saturday.

Conversely, the capital club are also unbeaten on their travels, collecting 14 points from a possible 18 and scoring a prolific 15 goals across six away matches, six more than their nearest challengers Marseille, Toulouse and Strasbourg.

The travelling supporters will therefore hope that their side's attacking proficiency serves them well at a ground where PSG have not lost since 2022, recording three victories during that period.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):.

Nice have several absentees ahead of Saturday's clash with PSG: Antoine Mendy (knee), Moise Bombito (leg), Laurent Abergel (knee) and Mohamed Abdelmonem (muscle) are all unlikely to feature.

Nonetheless, the Eaglets have several match-winners capable of troubling the defending Ligue 1 champions, with leading scorer Elye Wahi aiming to add to his six goals and two assists.

Three of Sofiane Diop's five direct goal involvements have come across the last three Ligue 1 matches, while Jonathan Clauss has scored or assisted in four of his last five top-flight appearances.

PSG may be the division's leading scorers, but Ferran Torres's four goals and Achraf Hakimi's three stand out among Enrique's attacking returns.

Marquinhos's three league goals are particularly notable, as are Ilya Zabarnyi's two in five appearances, placing the latter level with Mika Godts and Senny Mayulu.

However, Marquinhos is doubtful for Saturday due to a thigh injury, alongside Nuno Mendes, Ousmane Dembele, Maghnes Akliouche (calf), Desire Doue (hamstring) and Dro Fernandez (muscle), while Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (knee) remains a long-term absentee.

Diouf; Seidu, Ndayishimiye, Mandza; Clauss, Witsel, Boudaoui, Nkounkou; Diop, Amoura; Wahi.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:.

Safonov; Hakimi, Zabarnyi, Pacho, Hernandez; Neves, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Torres, Godts.

Nice's resurgence deserves considerable respect, but their defensive absences present an unwelcome complication against the division's most productive attack.

PSG have not lost at Allianz Riviera since 2022 and should have enough midfield control and attacking variety to extend their winning sequence without requiring a spectacular performance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 21:26.

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose has revealed Alex Scott will start at least one of the next three competitive matches.

Scott has not played for Bournemouth since September after sustaining a thigh injury in England’s 7-0 win over Croatia at the start of October.

The midfielder missed the next eight matches before he returned to the matchday squad for the 2-1 victory over Ipswich Town before the international window.

However, Rose opted against risking Scott at Portman Road, giving him the chance to build up his fitness over the two-week break.

Bournemouth will resume their campaign with a home meeting with Nottingham Forest on Saturday, before they head on their travels for games against Celta Vigo and Fulham in the Europa League and Premier League respectively.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s fixture, Rose has confirmed that Scott will start at least one of the next three matches for the Cherries.

According to recent reports, "We have many games in the upcoming weeks. Next week we have three games, so there are a lot of choices.” Rose remarked in Thursday’s pre-match press conference.

“For sure, he is going to start one game in this. We have to increase the match time step by step.".

Forward Junior Kroupi missed the first two months of the season after undergoing foot surgery in the summer.

As a result, Rose was keen to exercise caution when Kroupi returned to action last month, handing him four substitute appearances before he linked up with Zinedine Zidane's France squad.

Kroupi made his international debut in the 3-1 defeat to Italy before he scored his first goal for France in Sunday's 2-1 win over Turkey.

While both of those appearances came from the bench, Rose has now provided an update on whether Kroupi is in a position to start games.

"Junior is ready to get more match time and even to start," the Bournemouth boss said.

In regard to absentees, the Cherries are likely to be without Juanlu Sanchez, Julian Araujo and Alex Toth.

In a recent development, ‘I can completely understand that. I’ve been around a long time now and unfortunately I’ve had these nights a couple of times where the fans do react like that.

It has been revealed that ‘You have to let them do that and you also understand why they’re doing it. But I suppose if we’re trying to flip a positive on it, I think maybe the first five or six games under Steve Clarke were maybe similar where we had a lot of change in the squad, we were trying to build something, we were trying to integrate new people into a new squad and things like that.

In a recent development, ‘We’re trying to do that and we have to be positive about that. We need the young lads to feel comfortable around us. We need them to step up.

‘We need the older players to really help them in that and really, really step up. And that’s the only way we’re going to be successful.

‘We’ll still be positive because that’s the only way we know, and we know we can build something special. We’ve done it. We’ve been questioned a few times and bounced back and now we’re going to need to do it again with a newer squad.’.

Robertson admits that the adverse results have fed into a lack of harmony behind the scenes — a sharp contrast to the positivity which was palpable as the side qualified for the World Cup a year ago today.

Robertson understands why fans booed another dismal performance by Pocognoli's team.

‘I still think we need to work on it,’ he said. ‘We still need to get closer as a group again because — I don’t like looking at the past any more — but under Steve we had a really close-knit group where what we created was pretty special.

‘And that’s rare but we also have to try and do that again and we’re trying to make the latest players and the young lads feel as comfortable as possible. That’s the role of the older players and we have to keep doing that.

‘We have to keep encouraging them because they’re the ones that want to take us forward in years to come and they’re also the ones that are going to help us now.

‘Us older lads, we need to put a lot of responsibility on (ourselves) to try and help them do that, to try and keep pushing them, and we have to keep stepping up as well.

‘As a collective, we all need to step up more and if we do that then hopefully we can be successful again.’.

While the spotlight has largely fallen on the manager for persisting with a 3-4-2-1 formation, Robertson is adamant that it’s only fair the blame is shared around.

Sources indicate that ‘We all have to take responsibility,’ he mentioned. ‘Tactics and the way the manager sets us up and everything like that is one thing but then you’ve got 11  players, and we had 16 players, who have to go out and perform.

Skipper Robertson roars with anger and disbelief as Scotland team crumbles in Switzerland.

‘I don’t think we performed as a collective good enough. When you get beat 4-0, there’s not going to be any positives. There’s no fan in this stadium that’s going to go home and go: “We played well in the first half”.

‘That’s not how football works and we’re very aware of that. I’m very aware of that in terms of I don’t take any positives from a 4-0 defeat. I’m sorry but that’s the way I am and unfortunately that’s the way it is.’.

The Tottenham man became Scotland’s most capped player on Monday when he pulled on the jersey for the 103rd time, but that achievement was scant consolation at the time.

‘I’ve not given myself the chance to reflect,’ insisted Robertson. ‘In a couple of days’ time, probably when I unlock my phone and I get a couple of messages, I’ll realise what I’ve achieved and I don’t take it for granted.

‘I don’t take the magnitude of it for granted either, being able to overtake the legend of Kenny Dalglish. But it’s very hard to focus on myself after a result like that. I always focus on the team first and that’s always been my way.’.

#38061. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

Recent findings suggest that this particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

Recent findings suggest that as impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca mentioned. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

It has been revealed that allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was vital for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca stated.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

Industry observers note that FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

According to recent reports, nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

Sources indicate that all told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

In a recent development, great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

According to recent reports, A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Sources indicate that lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Massive cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Industry observers note that norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

Sources indicate that and Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

In a recent development, maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Industry observers note that some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

In a recent development, and without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Sources indicate that credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

According to recent reports, as we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Sources indicate that samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

Recent findings suggest that he has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

In a recent development, norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Sources indicate that samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Sources indicate that spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

Sources indicate that it’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:.

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré.

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a upcoming five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

According to recent reports, speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

Industry observers note that 17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

It has been revealed that his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

In a recent development, city fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

In a recent development, good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

Sources indicate that these two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

In a recent development, philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

Arsenal Women held by London City Lionesses despite Frida Maanum goal

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.
  • Recent findings suggest that frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game.
  • Arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

Arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

It has been revealed that arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

According to recent reports, arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

Latest Update: Mauricio Pochettino's record vs Liverpool: Can he overcome Reds litmus test on Man Utd managerial debut?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (825 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 21:29, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:08.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has taken the plunge into unfinished Premier League business, accepting the daunting challenge of taking charge of Manchester United at arguably the lowest ebb in their modern history.
  • Since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure, the Red Devils have endured a steady and, at times, bewildering decline, although few could have envisaged the club spiralling to such depths.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 21:29, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:08.

Mauricio Pochettino has taken the plunge into unfinished Premier League business, accepting the daunting challenge of taking charge of Manchester United at arguably the lowest ebb in their modern history.

Since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure, the Red Devils have endured a steady and, at times, bewildering decline, although few could have envisaged the club spiralling to such depths.

Sitting in the bottom three of the Premier League table after 10 games, Man Utd find themselves navigating one of the darkest chapters of their history in more than two decades.

Michael Carrick had offered plenty of promise last season after steering the club back into the Champions League, but that resurgence proved painfully short-lived, with the momentum failing to carry into the newly introduced campaign and the hierarchy eventually losing patience with the Englishman.

A total of 11 managers, including interim appointments, have come and gone since 2013, and while the Old Trafford hotseat retains its considerable allure, the red carpet awaiting its latest occupant has long since been replaced by a bed of nails.

By accepting the offer, Pochettino has willingly grasped the poisoned chalice, although he could yet emerge as the Red Devils' long-awaited Messiah if he is afforded the time and authority to mould the squad in his own image and build something capable of enduring.

A trip to Anfield represents the ultimate litmus test for any Manchester United manager, and Pochettino could hardly have been handed a more imposing introduction to life in the Old Trafford dugout.

The two most successful clubs in English football share a rivalry of extraordinary magnitude, one whose history, intensity and cultural significance are difficult to replicate anywhere else in Europe's major leagues.

Curiously, however, it has been a rarity for both sides to enjoy their periods of absolute dominance simultaneously, with the balance of power traditionally swinging one way before shifting back after a prolonged spell.

Liverpool ruled the roost throughout much of the 1970s and 1980s, before the Red Devils seized the mantle and established themselves as England's pre-eminent force over the following two decades.

That hierarchy has shifted once again, with Liverpool restoring their position among the country's leading powers and adding two more league titles to their illustrious collection.

Pochettino's immediate priority will be to drag Man Utd out of their current mire, but the longer-term ambition must surely extend beyond mere recovery: restoring the club's former stature and, ultimately, knocking Liverpool off their perch once again.

Across his managerial career, the 54-year-old has faced Liverpool 19 times, winning three, drawing five and suffering 11 defeats, a record that makes for sobering reading ahead of his latest meeting with the Reds.

One of those losses came on the grandest stage of all: the Champions League final, when Divock Origi struck the decisive goal to etch his name into Anfield folklore and condemn Pochettino's Tottenham Hotspur to defeat.

Curiously, however, some of the Argentine's most memorable moments against Liverpool came when he was managing Southampton.

Back in 2013, Pochettino, then still a relatively unheralded figure in English football, masterminded a tactical masterclass at Anfield, where Southampton suffocated Liverpool's attacking threat with an aggressive press executed with remarkable discipline and control.

The Saints emerged with a famous 1-0 victory, providing an early glimpse of Pochettino's tactical credentials before his subsequent move to north London.

His time at Tottenham, by contrast, proved considerably less fruitful against the Merseyside giants, with Pochettino managing just one victory in 13 meetings.

That solitary success came in emphatic fashion, as Spurs swept Liverpool aside 4-1 at Wembley Stadium during their temporary stay at the ground in the 2017-18 campaign, while he also oversaw a 1-1 draw against the Reds during his brief spell at Chelsea.

Few would blame Pochettino if Man Utd were to come away from Anfield empty-handed, particularly given the lack of time he has had to prepare his side for such a daunting assignment, while even a hard-fought draw would represent an excellent result.

Having arrived at Old Trafford at such a turbulent juncture, it would be unrealistic to expect the Argentine to weave his magic overnight, but the Red Devils arguably need him now more than he needs them, with the club crying out for direction, stability and a clearly defined footballing identity.

Through meticulous coaching, astute recruitment and, crucially, the unwavering backing of the hierarchy, Pochettino could gradually restore the foundations that have been missing for so long and give the Red Devils a genuine platform from which to rise again.

For now, though, the Argentine must resist the temptation to look too far ahead and simply embrace the challenge in front of him, because while the Anfield cauldron represents a formidable first examination, it also offers him an opportunity to make an early statement and begin a fresh chapter at Manchester United on his own terms.

Although Kudus has yet to score a league goal this season, the playmaker's three assists and ability to threaten from unlikely positions make him a potential match-winner for the home side.

Leading the line will be Dominic Solanke, who will look to capitalise on that creative service and spearhead the North Londoners to maximum points on Saturday afternoon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal are noted to be trying to reward Piero Hincapié with better contract terms after just months since making his move permanent.
  • Sources indicate that according to reports, negotiations are at an advanced stage between the Ecuadorian and international players.
  • In a recent development, however, Hincapié is in a slightly different position compared to his teammates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal are noted to be trying to reward Piero Hincapié with better contract terms after just months since making his move permanent.

Sources indicate that according to reports, negotiations are at an advanced stage between the Ecuadorian and international players. David Raya is also near to signing a new contract as Mikel Arteta looks to retain his key squad members.

In a recent development, however, Hincapié is in a slightly different position compared to his teammates. The 24-year-old only signed a five-year deal permanently in the summer.

Therefore, he could be discussing an increase in his salary rather than an extension. It has not been officially confirmed by either Arsenal or the player.

Arsenal have exercised their option to make Hincapié’s loan move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent.

Recent findings suggest that the defender made 39 appearances in all competitions during his first season in North London, scoring one goal and providing two assists. He has become an crucial part of Arteta’s defensive options.

His versatility has been an asset to Arsenal. His ability to play as a centre-back or left-back meaning he provides another option to utilise when problems occur with injuries or rotation in defence.

However, Hincapié has been overshadowed by Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori, making it a tough battle for playing time.

In the current campaign, he has played just five games in the league, with all of them coming off the bench. A total of 67 minutes has been played.

Hincapié will not be too concerned by this, as Arsenal have plenty of defensive options, and he provides cover in two positions.

The news that Hincapié is in talks is part of a bigger story around the club trying to keep their best players.

According to recent reports, declan Rice has signed a newly introduced five-year deal with Jurrien Timber, signing on improved terms. Raya is also said to be close to signing a new deal.

Arteta has already signed his future to the club until 2030. It is clear that they want to keep the continuity going forward after recent success.

While Hincapié has a contract until next year, renegotiating his deal would show how much Arsenal values him.

They may want to reward their players who have rapidly become key members of their squad.

Industry observers note that he has no reports of being unhappy and looking to leave the club. It seems he is being rewarded for his contributions to the club and to give him security in the long term.

This is a huge vote of confidence for a player who has only just completed his permanent move this summer.

#38051. Arsenal mourns Peter Storey: 1971 Double-winning hero dies aged 81

Arsenal mourns Peter Storey: 1971 Double-winning hero dies aged 81

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Readarsenal

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.
  • Recent findings suggest that storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history.
  • Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Recent findings suggest that storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

He was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Recent findings suggest that storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

It has been revealed that storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

Recent findings suggest that he played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

He will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

#38049. Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE2 production for tumour immune escape

Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE2 production for tumour immune escape

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 77 min read (15411 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~77 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, ferroptosis, a form of cell death induced by overwhelming membrane lipid peroxidation, is a vulnerability of many cancers, including cancers resistant to current molecular and immune-based therapies1,2,3,4,5,6,7.
  • Uncontrolled lipid peroxidation is integral to ferroptosis5,15.
  • Recent findings suggest that potentially relevant immunoregulatory factors produced by ferroptotic cancer cells are oxylipins, bioactive lipids generated through peroxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acid-containing membrane lipids, a hallmark of ferroptosis15.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ferroptosis, a form of cell death induced by overwhelming membrane lipid peroxidation, is a vulnerability of many cancers, including cancers resistant to current molecular and immune-based therapies1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Triggering of ferroptosis therefore provides an opportunity to achieve elimination of difficult-to-treat cancers1,2,3,4,8,9. Studies in mouse cancer models have demonstrated that anticancer immunity, mediated by dendritic cells (DCs) and CD8+ T cells, is essential for effective tumour eradication by ferroptosis-inducing strategies10,11,12,13. However, ferroptotic cells limit this response8,9,10,14, resulting in immune escape and tumour growth through mechanisms that remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program resulting in aberrant production of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), which limits the stimulation of anticancer CD8+ T cell responses by type 1 conventional DCs (cDC1s), thereby promoting immune escape. In ferroptotic cancer cells, lipid peroxidation-mediated membrane permeabilization enables Ca2+ influx, which activates p38 MAPK signalling and thereby drives PGE2 production. This signalling axis is uncoupled from cancer cell death and can be targeted to selectively interfere with immune-inhibitory PGE2 production while preserving ferroptotic cancer cell elimination. In the context of cancer cell ferroptosis, ablation of PGE2 production or disrupting PGE2 signalling restores cDC1-mediated anticancer CD8+ T cell responses and leads to effective tumour elimination. Our findings identify a key mechanism that limits antitumour immunity and prevents tumour elimination upon ferroptosis induction in cancer cells, which could be exploited for cancer therapy.

Uncontrolled lipid peroxidation is integral to ferroptosis5,15. Cancer cells are commonly protected from unrestrained lipid peroxidation and spontaneous ferroptotic cell death by molecular defence systems such as the system xc––glutathione (GSH)–glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) pathway5,16, in which GPX4 is the key enzyme mediating lipid peroxide detoxification. Strategies to promote ferroptosis by blockade of ferroptosis defence systems, such as GPX4 inhibitors, have been considered promising approaches to achieve tumour elimination in patients with difficult-to-treat cancers8,9. Studies using preclinical mouse models have uncovered that effective tumour elimination by ferroptosis-inducing strategies requires anticancer immunity by DCs10 and tumour-infiltrating CD8+ T cells11,12,13. Yet recent findings have suggested that DC-driven anticancer CD8+ T cell immunity is suppressed in ferroptotic tumours8,9,10,17. Emerging evidence has implicated that the unrestrained generation of membrane lipid peroxides in ferroptotic cells can promote the production and release of molecules that may impact immune cell functions18. However, what causes the suppression of DC-mediated anticancer CD8+ T cell immunity in the context of tumour ferroptosis remains largely unclear.

Recent findings suggest that potentially relevant immunoregulatory factors produced by ferroptotic cancer cells are oxylipins, bioactive lipids generated through peroxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acid-containing membrane lipids, a hallmark of ferroptosis15. To assess ferroptosis-induced oxylipin production and identify key factors, we profiled the oxylipin secretome of mouse BRAF(V600E) and NRAS(G12D) melanoma, 4T1 breast cancer and MC38 colorectal cancer cells following RSL3-induced ferroptosis. Across all these cancer cell lines, RSL3-treated (ferroptotic) cells displayed increased production of oxylipins compared with untreated (non-ferroptotic) controls (Fig. 1a). Of note, in all groups, the eicosanoid PGE2 was by far the most abundant oxylipin upregulated by ferroptosis induction (Fig. 1a). Similar to ferroptosis induction by RSL3 (which inhibits selenoproteins beyond GPX4), we observed strong PGE2 production after genetic ablation of the ferroptosis-protective enzyme GPX4, ferroptosis induction using the GPX4 inhibitor ML210 or erastin-mediated inactivation of system xc–-mediated cystine import (Extended Data Fig. 1a–f). Thus, ferroptosis may trigger the production of PGE2 in cancer cells, which is a notable finding given the important role of PGE2 for suppression of anticancer immunity19,20,21.

According to recent reports, by contrast, stimulation of ultraviolet B (UVB)-induced apoptosis, doxorubicin-induced immunogenic cell death or necrocide 1 (NC1)-induced necrotic cell death failed to promote PGE2 production (Fig. 1b and Extended Data Fig. 1g). However, PGE2 production was induced in cells undergoing necroptosis (Extended Data Fig. 1h). These findings imply that PGE2 production is selectively induced by as yet unknown molecular events in ferroptotic cells and that these events, at least to some extent, may be shared with necroptotic cells.

Using liproxstatin-1 (Lip-1), we further validated that ferroptotic cancer cells depend on lipid peroxides to produce PGE2 (Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). This was not the case for key effectors of other cell death pathways, such as caspases or receptor-interacting serine–threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1; Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). We extended our analyses to a broader panel of mouse and human cancer cells, including established cell lines, cells from spontaneous mouse cancer models and cells from patients with pancreatic cancer. In all these cells, RSL3-induced ferroptosis triggered markedly increased PGE2 production (Extended Data Fig. 2c–e). Together, these data suggest that ferroptosis promotes aberrant production of PGE2 in mouse and human cancer cells, prompting us to investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms and consequences for anticancer immunity.

Effective anticancer immunity often depends on cDC1s22,23, which fulfil essential roles in the priming of anticancer CD8+ T cell responses24,25 and effector differentiation and expansion of CD8+ tumour-infiltrating T lymphocytes (TILs)26,27. These cDC1 functions are impacted by immunoregulatory factors derived from dying cancer cells22,23,28; however, how mediators released by ferroptotic cancer cells impact cDC1s and their functions is not known.

To address this glitch, we generated cDC1s from bone marrow cells, exposed them to conditioned medium from RSL3-induced, ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) melanoma cells and assessed their functional properties after activation with polyinosinic–polycytidylic acid (poly(I:C); Fig. 1c). The conditioned medium from ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) cells strongly compromised the capacity of cDC1s to produce CXCL9 (Fig. 1d,e and Extended Data Fig. 3a), a chemokine required for cDC1-mediated orchestration of CD8+ TIL responses26,29. Similar results were observed for cDC1 production of the T cell stimulatory cytokine interleukin-12 (IL-12)30 (Extended Data Fig. 3b,c). By contrast, no impairment was observed for cDC1s exposed to conditioned medium from cancer cells undergoing apoptosis or doxorubicin-induced immunogenic cell death (Fig. 1d,e and Extended Data Fig. 3b,c). Impaired CXCL9 production was similarly observed for splenic cDC1s treated with conditioned medium from ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) cells (Extended Data Fig. 3d). These results suggest that factors released by ferroptotic cancer cells disable cDC1s from producing molecules required to promote anticancer CD8+ T cell immunity.

cDC1 functions are controlled by transcriptional programming31,32. We therefore subjected cDC1s activated by poly(I:C) following exposure to ferroptotic or apoptotic BRAF(V600E) cell conditioned medium to transcriptional profiling by RNA sequencing. We found that ferroptotic, but not apoptotic, cancer cell-derived factors induced prominent transcriptional changes in cDC1s (Fig. 1f), including impaired expression of genes encoding stimulatory cytokines (including Ifnb and Ifnl2), T cell-recruiting chemokines (Cxcl9 and Ccl4) and integrins vital for T cell activation (Itgal; Fig. 1f). We also confirmed the inhibitory effect on cDC1 cytokine and chemokine production at the protein level (Extended Data Fig. 3e). Of note, we did not detect a defect in upregulation of MHC or costimulatory molecules (Fig. 1f and Supplementary Table 1), implying that ferroptotic cancer cell-derived factors do not prevent cDC1 activation. Of note, many of the genes impaired in cDC1s following exposure to ferroptotic cancer cell-derived factors were shared with a core gene set of PGE2-mediated cDC1 dysfunction (Extended Data Fig. 3f,g and Supplementary Table 1), although genes beyond this set were also impaired. Consistently, gene set enrichment analyses revealed a prominent impairment of PGE2-regulated functional cDC1 genes (Extended Data Fig. 3h), whereas genes associated with migration or antigen processing (that is, molecular programs not regulated by PGE2 signalling in cDC1s19), remained unaffected (Extended Data Fig. 3h). Together, these data suggest that ferroptotic cancer cells promote cDC1 dysfunction and that this is mediated by PGE2.

Similar to cancer cells, ferroptosis induction caused aberrant PGE2 production in Pfa1 cells (Extended Data Fig. 4a), an established mouse embryonic fibroblast model often used to study the molecular underpinnings of ferroptosis33. This was linked to markedly increased transcript and protein expression of the key PGE2-producing enzyme COX2 (encoded by Ptgs2; Fig. 2a and Extended Data Fig. 4b–d). Lip-1 treatment rescued this effect (Fig. 2a), whereas stimulation of lipid peroxidation by cumene hydroperoxide promoted both Ptgs2 expression and increased PGE2 production in Pfa1 cells (Extended Data Fig. 4e,f). Together, these results point towards a requirement of membrane lipid peroxide generation for PGE2 production through transcriptional regulation of COX2. Using COX inhibitors, we also confirmed that COX activity was required for PGE2 production by ferroptotic Pfa1 cells (Fig. 2b), but dispensable for execution of ferroptotic cell death (Fig. 2c).

A key event caused by lipid peroxides in ferroptotic cells is the influx of extracellular Ca2+ (ref. 5), which constitutes an early event in pro-ferroptotic cells before the onset of cell death. Consistently, microscopy imaging revealed high intracellular Ca2+ levels in Pfa1 cells early after RSL3-mediated ferroptosis induction (Fig. 2d,e), which was similarly observed for multiple mouse cancer cells (Extended Data Fig. 4g,h). Time-resolved live cell imaging of ferroptotic Pfa1 cells confirmed that Ca2+ influx followed peroxide accumulation, but occurred before the cell death-associated loss of plasma membrane integrity (Fig. 2f). Of note, preventing Ca2+ influx through polyethylene glycol (PEG)-mediated blockade of membrane permeabilization-enabled osmotic molecule exchange5,34,35 (Fig. 2g and Extended Data Fig. 4i,j) abrogated the upregulation of Ptgs2 mRNA (Fig. 2h) and COX2 protein expression (Fig. 2i) in ferroptotic Pfa1 cells, resulting in a loss of PGE2 production (Fig. 2j). We also validated that lipid peroxide generation was only minimally affected by PEG treatment (Extended Data Fig. 4k,l) and that ferroptotic cells become permeable to other small extracellular molecules5, including sodium ions (Na+; Extended Data Fig. 4m–p).

Gain-of-function experiments using ionomycin, which selectively transport extracellular Ca2+ into cells, revealed that Ca2+ influx alone was sufficient to promote COX2 upregulation and PGE2 production across Pfa1, BRAF(V600E) melanoma and MC38 colorectal cancer cells (Extended Data Fig. 4q,r). Thus, although small molecules beyond Ca2+ enter ferroptotic cells, they probably do not contribute substantially to the activation of COX-mediated PGE2 production. Consistently, blockade of Ca2+ influx using the Ca2+ chelator EGTA confirmed the relevance of Ca2+ signalling for PGE2 production in ferroptotic cells (Fig. 2k and Extended Data Fig. 4s,t).

It has been revealed that ca2+ influx can regulate gene expression via p38 MAPK signalling, which requires p38 MAPK activatory phosphorylation (p-p38). Consistently, ferroptotic Pfa1 cells displayed a prominent increase in p-p38 levels (Fig. 2l,m), which was abolished by PEG treatment (Fig. 2l,m). Moreover, treatment with the selective p38 MAPK inhibitor SB203580 abrogated the upregulation of COX2 expression and PGE2 production in ferroptotic Pfa1 cells (Fig. 2n,o), demonstrating the relevance of p38 MAPK signalling for PGE2 production. Of note, the later execution of cell death remained unaffected by p38 MAPK inhibition (Fig. 2p) or blockade of Ca2+ influx (Extended Data Fig. 5a). These results suggest that Ca2+-induced p38 MAPK signalling is not required for ferroptotic cell death. We also confirmed that SB203580 did not induce cell death in non-ferroptotic cells (Extended Data Fig. 5a), and that the death of SB203580-treated ferroptotic Pfa1 cells was rescued by Lip-1 (Fig. 2q).

Oxylipin profiling revealed a selective requirement of p38 MAPK signalling for production of PGE2 and other COX-derived eicosanoids in ferroptotic Pfa1 cells (Fig. 2r), whereas other oxylipins remained largely unaffected. Similar to Pfa1 cells, PEG-mediated inhibition of Ca2+ influx or inhibition of p38 MAPK abolished PGE2 production in ferroptotic cancer cells (Extended Data Fig. 5b–e), demonstrating the relevance of Ca2+-mediated p38 MAPK pathway activation for PGE2 production also in ferroptotic cancer cells. We also confirmed that, in cancer cells, this mechanistic axis is already active in the early phase after ferroptosis induction (Extended Data Fig. 5f–r) and that p38 MAPK signalling is dispensable for the propagation of ferroptotic cell death (Extended Data Fig. 5s–v). Experiments with cells deficient in p38α (the p38 MAPK isoform commonly expressed in cancer cells) further validated that p38 MAPK signalling is required for PGE2 production by ferroptotic cancer cells (Extended Data Fig. 5w,x), but not their cell death execution (Extended Data Fig. 5y). We conclude that Ca2+-mediated activation of p38 MAPK signalling triggers PGE2 production by ferroptotic cells and that this mechanism is not required for ferroptosis-dependent cancer cell death (Fig. 2s). This molecular uncoupling enables to selectively interfere with p38 MAPK pathway activity to impair PGE2 production by ferroptotic cancer cells while preserving ferroptosis-mediated cancer cell elimination.

To test whether ferroptotic cancer cells depend on PGE2 to promote cDC1 dysfunction, we induced ferroptosis in COX-deficient Ptgs1/Ptgs2−/− BRAF(V600E) melanoma cells, which cannot produce PGE2 (Extended Data Fig. 6a–c). We then exposed cDC1s to conditioned medium from ferroptotic Ptgs1/Ptgs2−/− or control BRAF(V600E) cells, activated them by poly(I:C) and compared their gene expression profile by RNA sequencing (Fig. 3a). We also included cDC1s exposed to conditioned medium from apoptotic BRAF(V600E) cells, to test possible effects of dying cancer cell-derived factors unrelated to ferroptosis. We observed that PGE2 deficiency in ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) cells prevented cDC1 reprogramming (Fig. 3b) and, consequently, rescued the expression of functional cDC1 genes (for example, Irf8, Ifnl2 and Cxcl9; Fig. 3c). This regain of gene expression was similarly observed in a more detailed analysis of the core functional cDC1 genes selectively suppressed by factors from ferroptotic, but not apoptotic, BRAF(V600E) cells (Fig. 3d).

Recent findings suggest that the inhibitory effect of PGE2 on immune cells36, including cDC1s19, is mediated by signalling through the PGE2 receptors EP2 (encoded by Ptger2) and EP4 (encoded by Ptger4). We therefore extended our RNA sequencing analyses to EP2/EP4-deficient cDC1s from ItgaxcrePtger2−/−Ptger4fl/fl mice19,26. Whereas conditioned medium from PGE2-producing ferroptotic control BRAF(V600E) cells compromised the upregulation of activation induced genes in (EP2/EP4-proficient) wildtype (WT) cDC1s, this defect was fully rescued in EP2/EP4-deficient cDC1s (Fig. 3e and Supplementary Table 2). This result demonstrates the relevance of PGE2–EP2/EP4 signalling for ferroptotic cancer cell-mediated impairment of cDC1 functions. In separate experiments, we further validated that CXCL9 and IL-12 production is rescued in both EP2/EP4-deficient cDC1s treated with conditioned medium from ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) cells and cDC1s treated with conditioned medium from (PGE2-deficient) ferroptotic Ptgs1/Ptgs2−/− (BRAF(V600E)) cells (Fig. 3f,g and Extended Data Fig. 6d,e). Using CXCL9 as a functional marker, we also confirmed that PGE2 was similarly required for ferroptotic cancer cell-mediated inhibition of cDC1s activated by stimuli reported to promote cDC1 activation in tumours (Extended Data Fig. 6f,g). In a T cell stimulation assay, we further probed the ability of cDC1s to stimulate CD8+ T cell expansion. This function was similarly rescued in cDC1s exposed to conditioned medium from PGE2-deficient ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) cells (Fig. 3h,i). Using celecoxib (CXB)-mediated blockade of PGE2 production, we also confirmed that other ferroptotic cancer cells depend on PGE2 to inhibit cDC1 function, as determined by CXCL9 staining (Extended Data Fig. 6h,i). Together, these findings suggest that PGE2–EP2/EP4 signalling mediates the impairment of cDC1 functions caused by ferroptotic cancer cells. Moreover, EP2/EP4 deficiency rescues cDC1s from ferroptotic cancer cell-mediated inhibition.

Our results raised the question whether cDC1s can mount effective CD8+ T cell responses against ferroptotic cancer cells when protected from inhibitory PGE2 signalling. To address this issue, we adoptively transferred CD8+ OT-I T cells, which express a transgenic T cell receptor (TCR) specific for the model antigen ovalbumin (OVA), into WT mice subsequently transplanted with ferroptotic, OVA-expressing control or Ptgs1/Ptgs2−/− BRAF(V600E) cells (Extended Data Fig. 7a). To determine the relevance of EP2/EP4-mediated PGE2 signalling in cDC1, we further included Clec9acrePtger2−/−Ptger4fl/fl mice, which lack EP2 and EP4 in CLEC9A-expressing cDC1. Analyses of OT-I T cell expansion in lymphoid tissues revealed that ferroptotic cancer cell-derived PGE2 impairs the productive generation of anticancer CD8+ T cell responses through PGE2-mediated inhibition of cDC1 functions (Extended Data Fig. 7b–e). Moreover, OT-I T cell expansion was lost in cDC1-deficient Batf3−/− mice challenged with ferroptotic BRAF(V600E)–OVA cells (Extended Data Fig. 7f), confirming the functional relevance of cDC1s for generation of anticancer CD8+ T cell responses.

Sources indicate that to determine whether ferroptotic tumours depend on PGE2 production to restrict cDC1-mediated anticancer CD8+ TIL responses and escape immune control, we analysed the growth of (ferroptotic) Gpx4−/− or (non-ferroptotic) WT MC38 cells transplanted into WT and Clec9acrePtger2−/−Ptger4fl/fl mice (Fig. 4a). By microscopy-based analysis of the ferroptosis marker 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) and COX2 protein, we confirmed cancer cell ferroptosis leading to enhanced COX pathway activity in Gpx4−/−, but not WT, MC38 tumours (Extended Data Fig. 8). In WT mice, tumours formed by Gpx4−/− MC38 cells exhibited progressive tumour growth, which was only minimally slower than WT MC38 cells (Fig. 4b and Extended Data Fig. 9a). These data are consistent with inefficient control of ferroptotic cancers in immunocompetent mice. By contrast, Clec9acrePtger2−/−Ptger4fl/fl mice exhibited improved tumour immune control and fully rejected Gpx4−/− MC38 tumours (Fig. 4b and Extended Data Fig. 9a). By contrast, WT MC38 tumours displayed reduced growth but failed to be eliminated in Clec9acrePtger2−/−Ptger4fl/fl mice (Fig. 4b and Extended Data Fig. 9a). Of note, this pattern was similarly observed for Cd4crePtger2−/−Ptger4fl/fl mice in which T cells lack EP2/EP4 expression (Extended Data Fig. 9b), implying that ferroptotic tumours, in parallel to inhibiting cDC1, depend on PGE2-mediated inhibition of T cells to escape anticancer immunity.
