West Ham v Preston Preview: Team News & Lineups as Parker Faces Must-Win Home Debut

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1158 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham United v Preston North End EFL Championship London Stadium Saturday 21 November 2026, 3pm GMT.
  • In a recent development, scott Parker’s first home match as West Ham United head coach is massively vital.
  • Industry observers note that west Ham have collected one point from Parker’s opening two games and must start closing the gap to the automatic-promotion places.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United v Preston North End EFL Championship London Stadium Saturday 21 November 2026, 3pm GMT.

In a recent development, scott Parker’s first home match as West Ham United head coach is massively vital. Preston North End are bottom of the Championship and, while Saturday’s fixture is not mathematically must-win, realistically it feels very close to it.

Industry observers note that west Ham have collected one point from Parker’s opening two games and must start closing the gap to the automatic-promotion places. After two uninterrupted weeks with much of his squad, this is the first proper opportunity to judge whether the new head coach has begun improving the organisation and intensity of the team.

According to recent reports, there is also the troubling matter of West Ham’s home form. I worried before relegation that the vast gaps between the London Stadium crowd and the pitch might turn it into a disadvantage rather than an advantage, and we now desperately need to begin winning there consistently.

Recent findings suggest that the London Stadium has not remotely resembled a fortress this season. Opponents have arrived believing they can frustrate West Ham, exploit the anxiety around the ground and capitalise when the players become nervous.

In a recent development, as one former Championship striker recently observed, visiting teams have been enjoying the London Stadium experience. That situation has to change if West Ham are serious about challenging for automatic promotion.

It has been revealed that parker needs his players to begin quickly and give the crowd something to respond to. The longer this remains goalless, the more Preston will believe their long-ball approach and deep defensive shape can earn them something.

Scott Parker will need to make the London Stadium feel like home.

West Ham will dominate possession, so the challenge will be using it properly. Passing sideways in front of an organised defence will achieve very little; we need quicker movement, runners beyond the striker and enough tempo to pull Preston out of position.

In a recent development, I expect West Ham to be considerably tighter defensively following Parker’s first extended spell on the training pitch. However, the international break has not been quite as useful as it initially appeared because several important players were away representing their countries.

According to recent reports, konstantinos Mavropanos was among those absent, while Max Kilman is suspended after reaching the disciplinary threshold at Blackburn. Parker has therefore been unable to work throughout the fortnight with the central-defensive partnership he will need on Saturday.

I suspect Morato will move into his natural centre-back position alongside Mavropanos. That is probably the safe and predictable selection, although I would prefer to see Airidas Golambeckis given the opportunity.

The teenager has generally impressed when called upon and deserves serious consideration. As our examination of Parker’s defensive conundrum against Preston highlighted, the decision appears to be between Morato’s experience and Golambeckis’ encouraging performances.

Industry observers note that joël Veltman should start at right-back, while Ezra Mayers deserves to retain his place on the left. Kyle Walker-Peters continues to be assessed, but Parker has two natural and capable full-back options without needing to rush him back.

According to recent reports, the biggest selection question surrounds the goalkeeper. I am finding Parker’s team difficult to predict primarily because I do not know whether he will retain Mads Hermansen or turn to Alphonse Areola.

Hermansen has produced an inconsistent sequence of performances. He excelled for Denmark against Portugal before making another clanger during the defeat by Norway, which will not have made Parker’s decision any easier.

It has been revealed that there has been considerable pressure for West Ham to make a change in goal, but Areola’s own fitness has reportedly been an issue. Until Parker confirms otherwise, my best guess is that Hermansen will retain his place.

I suspect Parker will stick with Hermansen.

This is an ideal fixture in which to rebuild the goalkeeper’s confidence, but Preston’s likely use of long balls and set pieces means he must command his penalty area properly. Another nervous display would only intensify the debate but my own choice would be to select Finn Herrick.

I expect Parker to continue with the 4-2-3-1 formation. Arne Engels and Soungoutou Magassa should form the central-midfield partnership, with Divine Mukasa operating further forward.

Industry observers note that magassa gives West Ham a recognised holding midfielder and should help protect a changed defence. That will allow Engels to move the ball forward and support Mukasa rather than both central midfielders occupying similar positions.

Industry observers note that preston’s victory over Southampton was built around an aggressive pressing approach, something Parker will have worked on during the break. I previously argued that West Ham must learn to play through Preston’s press, and this midfield should contain enough composure and energy to do it.

It has been revealed that jarrod Bowen will naturally start on the right, with Edvin Austbø on the left. In my opinion, Austbø has moved ahead of Manor Solomon in the pecking order and deserves a proper run in the team.

Joël Piroe should lead the attack. Parker needs to give West Ham’s most proven Championship goalscorer an extended opportunity rather than continually rotating strikers who have struggled to find any rhythm.

Industry observers note that I expect five players who were away on international duty—Hermansen, Mavropanos, Mukasa, Austbø and Piroe—to start. The key defensive change should see Morato move inside to replace the suspended Kilman.

Sources indicate that preston earned their first victory under Graham Alexander by beating Southampton before the international break, so they should arrive with renewed confidence. However, both of their Championship wins this season have come at home.

Their away record is dreadful. Preston are winless on the road, having drawn once and lost six of their seven away league matches, including some heavy defeats.

According to recent reports, I expect them to use plenty of long balls, remain compact and try to frustrate West Ham. Even so, the Hammers have far better players and will enjoy the lion’s share of possession.

Quite frankly, it is time they indicated the difference in quality. If West Ham cannot beat the Championship’s bottom club at home after Parker has been given two weeks to prepare, serious questions will remain about our promotion credentials.

Preston may make the opening stages awkward, but West Ham should eventually have far too much attacking quality. Parker’s team need to play with intensity, move the ball rapidly and turn possession into genuine chances rather than merely dominating the statistics.

In a recent development, I expect a much more organised performance following the international break. Preston’s direct approach may still produce a goal, particularly with West Ham fielding a changed central defence, but this should be the afternoon Parker claims his first victory.

Prediction: West Ham United 4-1 Preston North End.

Full fixture information is available through West Ham United’s official match centre.

German Giants Eye West Ham Star But Face £22m Obstacle

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham United midfielder Arne Engels is attracting interest from Bundesliga side VfB Stuttgart, although the German club could struggle to afford the £22m summer signing.
  • Sources indicate that according to German newspaper BILD, as reported by Sport Witness, Stuttgart have identified Engels as one of several potential replacements for Angelo Stiller, who could leave the club next summer.
  • Industry observers note that however, Stuttgart reportedly regard the cost of signing Engels as unrealistic, with West Ham unlikely to accept a substantial loss on a player who only arrived from Celtic in August.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United midfielder Arne Engels is attracting interest from Bundesliga side VfB Stuttgart, although the German club could struggle to afford the £22m summer signing.

Sources indicate that according to German newspaper BILD, as reported by Sport Witness, Stuttgart have identified Engels as one of several potential replacements for Angelo Stiller, who could leave the club next summer. Southampton’s Caspar Jander and Middlesbrough’s Aidan Morris are also under consideration.

Industry observers note that however, Stuttgart reportedly regard the cost of signing Engels as unrealistic, with West Ham unlikely to accept a substantial loss on a player who only arrived from Celtic in August. The German club previously wanted the Belgian during his time at Augsburg, so this is not an entirely fresh interest.

Look, clearly Engels is somebody that West Ham head of recruitment Nils Koppen values extremely highly.

Sources indicate that as we reported when the £22m agreement with Celtic was reached, the Belgian had been Koppen’s primary midfield target throughout much of the summer. West Ham pursued him for weeks before finally getting their man.

I thought very quickly he’d become one of the first names on the team sheet under Nuno Espírito Santo, and I suspect that will continue under Scott Parker.

So clearly he is a player who is admired.

That stated, I’m not surprised Stuttgart are struggling to find value at £22m because I do think West Ham overpaid when we bought him from Celtic.

West Ham midfielders will play with more freedom under Parker which could unlock Engels value.

Now, that price becomes fully justified if he helps get the team promoted this season. If not, then I’d have to say that so far he’s done little to justify the price tag.

Recent findings suggest that that’s not to suggest Engels is a bad player. He’s a busy, high-energy midfielder who covers plenty of ground and contributes to the team’s overall play.

But there’s a difference between being a good Championship midfielder and looking like a £22m player.

Indeed, when I recently assessed Koppen’s summer recruitment, Engels was one of the players I felt remained something of an unknown quantity in terms of value for money.

But, and here’s the important thing, West Ham manager Scott Parker has a habit of getting central midfielders scoring goals.

And if he can get Engels further up the pitch than Nuno Espírito Santo managed to, and into goalscoring positions, I suspect his value will rise if he becomes a goalscorer rather than just a busy, high-energy midfield player.

We’ve already had a glimpse of what might be possible.

Engels scored his first West Ham goal during the extraordinary 3-3 draw at Cardiff City in Parker’s opening match, as the Hammers recovered from three goals down at half-time.

That was one of the positives from a remarkable second-half performance, which I discussed in my player ratings following the Cardiff comeback.

It has been revealed that however, against Blackburn, Parker used Engels in a deeper midfield role, with Mohamadou Kanté and Divine Mukasa operating further forward. As our Blackburn match report highlighted, that arrangement helped protect the defence but offered Engels fewer opportunities to get forward.

It will be interesting to see whether Parker can find a balance between the two.

Engels has the energy to get around the pitch, and if he can add regular goals to his game, the argument over whether West Ham paid too much could begin to look very different.

For now, Stuttgart’s interest looks more like an indication of Engels’ standing in the game than an immediate threat to West Ham.

The Belgian is under contract until 2031, with the club holding an option for another year, as confirmed by West Ham’s official website.

And with the Hammers attempting to win promotion at the first attempt, I can’t imagine Koppen being particularly enthusiastic about losing the player he worked so hard to sign.

Personally, I still believe £22m was too much money for what Engels has shown us so far.

But if Parker can turn him into a midfielder who regularly arrives in the penalty area and contributes goals, that assessment could change considerably.

And if those goals help West Ham get promoted, nobody will be complaining about the transfer fee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has admitted that Alphonse Areola is unlikely to be available for Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, leaving the Hammers with a familiar goalkeeping dilemma.

Speaking during his pre-match press conference, Parker explained that the club had attempted to push the Frenchman’s recovery but were struggling to get him ready.

“We tried to push it a bit, but it looks a little bit unlikely and we’ll leave it as long as we can before making a decision,” said the West Ham boss.

In a recent development, this isn’t particularly surprising. It’s something we’ve discussed previously on Claret & Hugh, with concerns surrounding Areola’s match fitness and reports that he has been carrying too much weight.

And considering Parker has worked with the Frenchman before, one has to assume he’d be really keen to play him.

The fact that he isn’t selecting Areola suggests the goalkeeper simply isn’t ready for action, particularly following his recent injury setback.

Personally, my choice would be to give young Fin Herrick a chance.

I was speaking to my Hammers Chat counterpart Geo during our West Ham v Preston preview this week, and he made an excellent observation.

The one thing Mads Hermansen has consistently been good at is his distribution with the ball at his feet.

Unfortunately, his clanger for Denmark in their last game means even that aspect of his performances is now under scrutiny.

He’s got the yips: West Ham goalkeeper Mads Hermansen, whose recent performances have raised concerns about his confidence.

I actually think the best thing we could possibly do for Hermansen would be to give him a rest.

His confidence has clearly taken a battering, and his latest international mistake has only increased the pressure.

Let’s be fair, young Herrick can’t perform any worse than the Danish keeper has in the last few games.

And as our recent coverage of supporters’ goalkeeping preferences demonstrated, there is already considerable dissatisfaction with the current situation.

I appreciate throwing a youngster into such an key game carries risks, but there comes a point when continuing with an out-of-form goalkeeper becomes an equally significant gamble.

For me, Saturday presents an opportunity to try something different.

#37999. Breaking: Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin

Breaking: Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1664 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1. These networks are among the stiffest found in the cytoskeleton and can generate large pushing stresses against stationary obstacles2,3,4,5. When grown against a controlled opposing stress in an atomic force microscope6 or inside the cell7, branched networks alter their own architecture to adapt their compressional stiffness to their environment, but the underpinnings of their mechanics and adaptability are unclear. Here we show that their high density and low connectivity place them outside the scope of standard elastic network models for actin. We show that they are instead dominated by the proliferation of interfilament contacts under compression. This places branched actin in the same category as undercoordinated fibrous materials such as sheep’s wool. When the network is grown under force, filaments entangle as if knitted together and trap contacts in their structure. Trapped contacts have a similar role as crosslinkers in rigidifying the network and are thus key to its active adaptive mechanics.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has spoken positively about Joël Piroe ahead of Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, raising an interesting question over his starting striker.

During his pre-match press conference, Parker acknowledged the Dutchman’s impressive goalscoring record and revealed that he was looking forward to spending more time working with him.

“I’ve known about Joël, having played against his teams. His goalscoring record is really good,” mentioned Parker.

“It’s a shame for us he’s been away, but he’s in good form, and I’m looking forward to working with him more.”.

Personally, I would 100% start Piroe ahead of Taty Castellanos, irrespective of how well the Argentine might have trained during the international break.

Piroe is a proven Championship goalscorer, and Parker knows all about him from his previous experience managing in this division.

I think he very much deserves a run of games in an attempt to fire at least one of our strikers into action.

The alternative is to continue persevering with Castellanos, who has been a considerable disappointment since West Ham’s relegation.

And there is another factor to consider.

As Claret & Hugh exclusively revealed, the club are exploring the possibility of selling Castellanos in January, with Nils Koppen already investigating potential replacements.

Further reports from Argentina have suggested the striker wants to leave, although no departure has been agreed.

Piroe is admired by Scott Parker.

I don’t think there’s any mystery surrounding what Piroe offers.

He knows the Championship, he knows how to score goals in it, and he’s already demonstrated that he can contribute to this West Ham team.

As we’ve previously argued when discussing Parker’s selection options, Piroe has a compelling case to start ahead of Castellanos.

Of course, the manager will have his own ideas about how he wants his centre-forward to play.

But given the lack of goals from our recognised strikers, I’d rather see Parker give the Dutchman a proper opportunity than continue waiting for Castellanos to discover some form.

For me, Piroe starts against Preston.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mark Noble has provided an interesting insight into how West Ham United’s recruitment operation is working under Scott Parker, revealing that Nils Koppen is in regular contact with the coaching staff about the players the club needs.

Speaking in an interview with West Ham’s official website, Noble explained that the Director of Player Recruitment is arriving at Rush Green as early as 6.30am, watching training and discussing the squad with Parker and his coaches.

In a recent development, with the January transfer window approaching and West Ham desperate to secure promotion, it’s encouraging to hear that recruitment discussions are taking place. But for me, the most crucial part of Noble’s revelation has very little to do with what time Koppen arrives for work.

Quite frankly, whether Koppen arrives at half six in the morning is neither here nor there.

Much of the analytical and recruitment work can be carried out perfectly well from wherever somebody can plug into the internet.

What I find far more vital is the open dialogue Noble has described.

He explained that Koppen watches training and that the coaching staff speak openly with him about the players they believe West Ham need.

Koppen then works with the club’s scouts and analysts in the background, allowing Parker and Noble to concentrate on coaching.

That strikes me as a huge plus and potentially a massive step in the right direction.

It also appears to represent a departure from the way things have operated previously, when questions were regularly raised about whether recruitment decisions matched the manager’s requirements.

As we discussed following Parker’s talkSPORT interview, the manager is absolutely right to concentrate on improving the players already at his disposal rather than becoming consumed by January transfers.

But that only works if the recruitment department understands precisely what he needs.

We know from our recent dialogue with a club insider that Koppen has begun looking for another striker, and Noble’s comments suggest those discussions are taking place alongside the coaching staff’s assessment of the squad.

That’s exactly how it should work.

Ultimately, I’m far more interested in whether Koppen signs the right players than whether he’s the first person through the door at Rush Green.

But if the people coaching the team and those recruiting for it are finally speaking openly about what West Ham need, that has to be encouraging.

According to recent reports, west Ham return to action tomorrow with a home tie against visitors Preston North End – a team who sit rock bottom of the Championship but are not without their recent triumphs after turning over promotion-chasing Southampton just before the break. So West Ham need to be wary, despite their opponents’ lowly league table position.

With Scott Parker having enjoyed an unbroken two week training period during the break, West Ham fans will now surely get to see the ‘Parker XI’ rather than Nuno’s inherited lin-up with which he began the first two games of his West Ham tenure.

The first visible difference will surely be to see -shock, horror – players used in their correct positions: Nuno because infamous for using square pegs in round holes – Morato at left back being the case in point.

Morata’s days at left back are surely over.

Despite being signed as a centre back and having played all but 33 of his last 177 games as such, Nuno insisted on using the 6’3 Brazilian – hardily the most mobile – as a left back who was frequently found to be out of position, often allowing wingers to get the better of him: Scott Parker hooked him at half time after a pretty inept left-back performance against Cardiff.

With centre back Maximilian Kilman suspended for tomorrow’s clash there should be no more Morato at left back – incredibly West Ham fans have never seen the loanee in his preferred specialist position until now. Ezra Mayers has already done enough to start at left back leaving Parker free to slot Morato into the role for which he was signed, alongside Mavropanos.

Square pegs into square holes: Scott Parker’s secret weapon in his West Ham reboot. Who’d have thought.

How Mauricio Pochettino's culture shock tactics will resurrect Man United: From 'Murderball' training that leaves players throwing up to telling Harry Kane to slim down and why even the smell of the kit must be spot on

  • When the entertaining but ultimately rather pointless Ralf Rangnick was tasked with holding the fort as manager at Manchester United five years ago, he was asked whether his much-admired style of football – the high-intensity gegenpress aped by disciples such as Jurgen Klopp – could work with a team that had Cristiano Ronaldo, 36, and Edinson Cavani, 34, in it.
  • Rangnick replied that he was certain it could.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 21:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 17 November 2026.

When the entertaining but ultimately rather pointless Ralf Rangnick was tasked with holding the fort as manager at Manchester United five years ago, he was asked whether his much-admired style of football – the high-intensity gegenpress aped by disciples such as Jurgen Klopp – could work with a team that had Cristiano Ronaldo, 36, and Edinson Cavani, 34, in it.

Rangnick replied that he was certain it could. The German was, of course, proved very wrong.

It is this kind of strange, blinkered hubris that we should not expect Mauricio Pochettino to bring with him to Old Trafford.

Heaven knows we have seen enough of that in recent times. Ruben Amorim and his back three. Erik ten Hag and… well maybe one day we will understand what all that was supposed to be about.

Recent findings suggest that but no, this will not be Pochettino. This cannot be Pochettino.

In a recent development, this United squad is not one built for the upcoming United manager’s favoured kind of front-foot, hurrying and harrying football. This is not Tottenham Hotspur 2016. It is not Kyle Walker, Toby Alderweireld, Son Heung-min and Harry Kane. It is not physical and youthful and energetic.

Mauricio Pochettino is waving goodbye to the US national team and hello to Man United this week. But he faces a daunting task at Old Trafford.

This United squad is not one built for the fresh United manager’s favoured kind of front-foot, hurrying and harrying football.

That is why Pochettino’s battle – at least for the remainder of this season – will be about hearts and minds as much as it is about anything revolutionary that he can bring to bear on the training fields of Carrington.

According to recent reports, the good news for those hoping for quick improvement is that Pochettino – at least the one who took Spurs to a Champions League final in 2019 and to within a sniff of a Premier League title a few years earlier – is adept at the mental and emotional side of football. It is upon this that, initially at least, he may wish to rely.

Son told me about this when we sat down to look back on his career in England. He was prolific under Pochettino, a scorer of 75 goals in four-and-a-half seasons under the Argentine. But it was not always like that. Once – just like several current players at United – he was disaffected and unhappy.

‘Mauricio turned me round and it wasn’t about football,’ Son told me. ‘It was about me as a person and how he made he feel.

According to recent reports, ‘I needed help, basically. And he gave me it.

'He did so many good things that I can't even say the words. It was unbelievable.

‘Sometimes he had been my coach and sometimes he had been like my family.’.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino inherits a jigsaw puzzle with the wrong-shaped pieces at Old Trafford. It’s a squad put together for and by six different managers.

Pochettino will want to improve the fitness levels at United and his intense methods might feel like an ice bath to their players.

'He did so many good things that I can't even say the words,' says Son Heung-min of his manager at Tottenham. 'It was unbelievable... sometimes he was like my family’.

On arrival this week, for example, he will renew acquaintances with Luke Shaw, one of his old Southampton players signed for Louis van Gaal at United back in 2014. Shaw – the club’s only real left back – is 31 now and recovering from injury.

The physical limitations of this United team were clear in the titanic but ultimately rather pitiful 4-4 draw with Aston Villa that proved to be Michael Carrick’s last game in charge just before the international break.

Industry observers note that invited back into a game they trailed 2-0, United’s front four briefly chased the life out of Villa when Unai Emery’s team were in possession. For 20 minutes, Villa could not get out of their own half.

But the likes of Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo simply could not maintain that level of exertion once the surge in adrenaline had spiked. By the time the game reached the hour mark, United were 4-2 down.

It is certain Pochettino will wish to improve some levels of fitness at United and his methods will perhaps feel like an ice bath to some of those United players who have approached the basic prerequisite of running like some kind of optional extra at times this season.

At Spurs, players were occasionally known to vomit during training. Pochettino told Harry Kane he could be the best striker in the world but not until he lost weight.

In a recent development, six or seven years later at Chelsea, meanwhile, he punished striker Nicolas Jackson for picking up five largely needless yellow cards by ordering him to run laps of the training pitch. Jackson was only told why it was happening as he lay on the grass in a heap afterwards.

Pochettino took many of his principles from his compatriot and former manager Marcelo Bielsa whose ‘Murderball’ sessions eventually arrived in England during his spell at Leeds United eight years ago. The stated aim is simple.

The likes of Bruno Fernandes (centre) have struggled to maintain the physicality Pochettino will demand across 90 minutes in games this season.

Pochettino took many of his principles from his compatriot and former manager Marcelo Bielsa.

‘With Mauricio, there is no hiding,’ remarked former Southampton midfielder Adam Lallana on the Rest Is Football podcast.

‘Everything is high-intensity, pressing from the front, and repeating sprints again and again in training so that it becomes automatic on a Saturday.’.

Trawl through Pochettino’s time as a frontline coach and the testimonies of unstinting, high-intensity work are strikingly similar. There has been no great change in the belief, even when he arrived in America to coach the US national team ahead of this summer’s World Cup.

In a recent development, 'He brings that club intensity into the national team environment,’ claims Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie. ‘You immediately feel the tempo he expects.’.

For this to work well, a coach needs two things. A pre-season in which to embed that specific kind of fitness and a squad assembled to play that way.

Recent findings suggest that at United, Pochettino has neither so we can expect it to be a slow burn. He is approaching the busiest period of the playing schedule – his team will play 12 games in the next six and a half weeks – and has immobile central defenders, full backs with limitations and a midfield unit that lacks legs when compared to the best in the Premier League and Europe.

Equally, Pochettino arrives back in a Premier League where many teams now trade off the same high-press principles that were once rather upcoming. Ten years ago, it was Klopp’s Liverpool. Now it’s Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton and many, many others.

Every player has a brain and a mind, though, and it is here that Pochettino will in all likelihood seek to make the greatest gains ahead of Sunday’s trip to Liverpool and beyond.

Pochettino arrives back in a Premier League where many teams now trade off the same high-press principles that were once rather newly introduced when he landed at Southampton in 2013.

Pochettino can be blunt with players. He told Harry Kane he could be the best striker in the world but not until he lost weight.

There is not a United manager since the end of the Sir Alex Ferguson era who has not run into trouble with individual players at some point. Ten Hag with Ronaldo, Jadon Sancho and Raphael Varane. Amorim with Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo. Carrick with his captain, Fernandes.

In a recent development, this, as much as anything, is what has held United back this season. United do not have a squad fit to win the league but that it sits in the bottom three says everything for the way Carrick and his coaching staff failed at their side of the deal.

Pochettino’s friendship with Ferguson is more than a decade old and endures. Ferguson will be thrilled at the appointment. Indeed, there are similarities to be found between the two. Pochettino, for example, is a small details man, a coach who understands that mood and motivation and cohesion can be just as important as tactics or indeed anything the opposition can bring on a Saturday afternoon.

Having reached out yesterday to a former Southampton player for input on his ex-manager’s methods, the former international gave an insight – albeit unwittingly – into the kind of loyalty Pochettino can inspire.

Sources indicate that ‘We need to let him integrate at United his own way,’ came the reply. ‘I don’t think he needs us talking about his secrets.’.

Pochettino can be blunt with players. He was with Son. He was with Kane.

‘He said, “You need to do this and this and that’s why you’re not in the squad”,’ Kane once told Daily Mail Sport. ‘And it just hit me. This is what I’ve got to do.’.

Equally, the 54-year-old trades in subtlety. At Tottenham, he would sit at the entrance to the training ground canteen to gauge his players’ state of mind as they walked in. He had staff video them at training and wondered why they always looked happier when they walked off at the end.

At Tottenham, Pochettino would sit at the entrance to the training ground canteen to gauge his players’ state of mind as they walked in.

According to recent reports, pochettino’s friendship with Sir Alex Ferguson is more than a decade old and endures. Ferguson will be thrilled at the appointment.

As strange as it sounds, Pochettino chose the detergent in the washing room as he believed the smell of the first team kit was key. He dropped a player simply because he had noticed him eating stodgy food before sessions and another because he believed his choice of car to be inappropriate to his relative lowly standing in the game.

In a recent development, these are the kinds of things that look clever when you win and like upcoming-age bunkum when you don’t. At Spurs, Pochettino’s results spoke for him but what is critical now is what version has walked through the door at Old Trafford.

It’s true that, to a large extent, we all view him as Pochettino 2016. In the decade that has followed, there have been underwhelming spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. His attempts at making the kind of emotional connections he thrives on in Paris, for example, soon ran into a brick wall with the words ‘Neymar’ and ‘Mbappe’ written on it.

To return to the Ferguson link again, Pochettino has not previously been shy of perceived similarities.

According to recent reports, ‘Ferguson used to tell his players that working hard is a talent,’ he wrote in his 2017 book Brave New World. ‘To me, if a player doesn’t work hard for the team, he won't play. Nothing happens by chance.’.

What manager in football doesn’t value basic endeavour? Not one but, as mutual trust and shared belief starts to wane during a run of bad results, even the basics can get lost. With this in mind and with Pochettino’s energy and charisma in the building, it’s not unrealistic to expect a new manager bounce at Old Trafford.

His relationship with Fernandes will be crucial and the Portuguese should not expect the captaincy to be a given. At Tottenham, Pochettino gave it to his goalkeeper, Hugo Lloris.

Pochettino knows that coaches can’t speak to players the way they used to, or indeed may wish to. A greater degree of emotional intelligence is required.

Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez - both publicly critical of the set-up at United this season - can expect private words of advice from their upcoming boss.

Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford a wiser manager for working amid the background noise at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea.

United’s players can therefore expect WhatsApp messages at 11pm at night – sometimes including attachments of training clips – quiet words of advice or observation when passing their manager in a corridor or even a short note, serious or otherwise, left in a dressing room locker. How the likes of Fernandes, Cunha, Rashford, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez respond to all this will be key.

So, too, will Pochettino’s ability or otherwise to make the best of the clunky chain of executive command that sits above him. At Tottenham, Pochettino and chairman Daniel Levy hit a sweet spot that wasn’t to last but for a time saw them so in tune they even took a horse-riding trip together. It was a synchronicity that electrified the whole football club.

Here in Manchester in 2026-27, it will feel different. At United, senior players criticise executives to the media while the fans wave green-and-gold scarves on matchday and sing unpleasant songs about not one but two different ownership groups. None of that will go away just because yet another manager is through the door.

Pochettino may feel he has some experience of such background noise from his time at PSG and indeed Chelsea. Equally, much of what happens over the course of the rest of this season and, if he is lucky, beyond will depend on his own reserves of energy, desire and self-regeneration. Does his own well remain deep enough?

The man who swept into Southampton with little-to-no English but bags of ideas and energy in January 2013 was an irresistible force of nature and he ran hot through the Premier League for a while. If he brings some of that to Old Trafford then he has a chance of making an impression at least.

In a recent development, but Pochettino’s take on Murderball, punishment laps and the infamous ‘Gacon’ 5km running drill he has been known to use may have to wait until the summer. United’s immediate complications, he will find, are more about a failing culture, centring less on playing style and more on emotional substance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 23:48, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 01:22.

AFC Wimbledon will be looking to claim a second straight win when they make the short trip to Brisbane Road for Saturday's League One clash against Leyton Orient.

The O's, meanwhile, are bidding to record a fourth consecutive home victory in all competitions.

Leyton Orient head into the weekend in 14th spot in the League One table after recording five wins, two draws and six defeats in their 13 league games this term.

Orient cruised to a 3-0 victory in their most recent league outing against Cambridge United at the end of October, a result that has formed part of a three-game winning run on home turf.

Their last victory at Brisbane Road took place in the FA Cup first round, which saw Idris El Mizouni net a brace in an emphatic 5-1 win over sixth-tier Harborough Town to set up a second-round tie against Port Vale.

However, Richie Wellens's side were unable to repeat that sort of success in their away clash against Barnet in the EFL Trophy, falling to a 4-2 defeat as they finished at the bottom of Group F and behind third-place Wimbledon on goal difference.

Orient will now return to the familiar surroundings of Brisbane Road, where they have won four of their last five outings, including three victories without conceding in their previous four home league games.

That represents a significant improvement from the start of the season when they lost each of their opening three home matches in the third tier.

Wimbledon have played a game more than Orient, but they are a point worse off after winning four, drawing four and losing six of their 14 League One matches.

In fact, the Dons have lost four of their previous six games in the third tier, although they did manage to end an 11-game winless run in all competitions in their most recent outing against Blackpool.

Alistair Smith's first-half proved enough to fire Wimbledon to a 1-0 victory, representing their first three-point haul since recording back-to-back wins against Bromley and Doncaster Rovers in September.

After enjoying success at Plough Lane, Johnnie Jackson's side will now make the trip to Brisbane Road for the second time this season after playing out a 1-1 draw in August's EFL Trophy encounter.

They missed out on a bonus point with a defeat in the subsequent penalty shootout, but they enjoyed greater success in January's league visit, when they fought back from a goal down to claim a 3-1 victory.

However, their hopes of repeating that success may be tempered by the fact they have lost six of their last eight competitive away games, including each of their last four.

Leyton Orient form (all competitions):.

AFC Wimbledon form (all competitions):.

Orient midfielder Ollie O’Neill will be out for around four months after undergoing an operation not long after returning from a long injury absence.

The hosts are also expected to be without the services of Nicholas Oyekunle, Demetri Mitchell and Sean Clare.

Rarmani Edmonds-Green will feature alongside Alfie Gilchrist in central defence after returning from injury to start the wins over Cambridge and Harborough.

As for the visitors, Wimbledon are unable to call upon Josef Bursik, Dan Sweeney, Dujuan Richards, Ryan Johnson and Donnell McNeilly due to injury.

Jayden Stockley will serve a one-match ban after being sent off for two bookable offences in the narrow win over Blackpool.

Aaron Sasu could move forward to replace Stockley in the frontline, which would open the door for Steven Sessegnon to feature at left wing-back.

Leyton Orient possible starting lineup:.

Baxter; Stevens, Edmonds-Green, Gilchrist, Boniface; El Mizouni, Gilbert; Connolly, Wellens, Dobra; Kabia.

AFC Wimbledon possible starting lineup:.

Bishop; Tilley, Yiadom, Ogundere, Seddon, Sessegnon; Smith, Harrison, Maycock; Cornick, Sasu.

Leyton Orient have made Brisbane Road a fortress in recent times, and considering Wimbledon have lost five of their seven away league games this season, we think the signs point to a home win on Saturday.

Industry News: West Ham’s Home Advantage Problem Won’t Disappear With 60,000 Fans

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.
  • Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.
  • Industry observers note that he also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.

Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.

Industry observers note that he also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage. But I think it’s notable to point out that getting the fans onside and creating an intimidating atmosphere are probably two very different things.

There’s no doubt about it. When the London Stadium is loud, it is impressive, as anybody who attended that incredible night against Sevilla will testify.

But I do think it’s a long way from being intimidating.

For that to happen, I firmly believe supporters need to be close to the pitch.

Not just to cause opposition players discomfort, but to put pressure on referees and give West Ham the kind of home advantage that seems prevalent throughout the league.

The distance between the stands and the playing surface remains a fundamental problem, regardless of how many supporters are in attendance.

It’s something I’ve previously argued when discussing proposals to improve the stadium atmosphere.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium.

In a recent development, it was always my concern that relegation to the Championship would see visiting teams regard a trip to the London Stadium as a lovely day out in opulent surroundings. Opposition changing rooms are grand and palatial and their team coach can pull into the venue untroubled by home fans.

Sources indicate that and our results in Stratford have certainly done little to disprove that theory. However, that doesn’t mean things can’t improve.

I genuinely believe that getting West Ham playing on the front foot will help eliminate some of the eerie silences we’ve heard so frequently at the London Stadium.

Noble wants supporters to see a team giving everything, and I think he’s absolutely right about that.

If Parker can produce an aggressive, attacking side that gives the crowd something to get excited about, the atmosphere should improve considerably.

But turning the London Stadium into a genuinely intimidating venue is another matter entirely.

And unfortunately, that’s a problem which can’t be solved simply by asking 60,000 people to make more noise.

Nuno Espirito Santo’s training sessions criticised today in revealing latest report.

Which begs the question “Just what were the squad working on under Nuno”?

It has been revealed that according to their new Manager, the changes he’s made have kicked in and there’s been a noticeable upturn. Which, lets face it, was long overdue, and after the new head coach’s first two games in charge was clearly, sorely needed.

According to recent reports, we’ll all see for ourselves tomorrow when Preston North End visit: After his tough two-game baptism of fire, Parker got his two week break to prepare for a home tie against the bottom side. Which is as easy as it’s going to get this season.

More than just a football club: Cardinale’s vision to make AC Milan a multi-billion empire

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has major plans for AC Milan.
  • Industry observers note that the RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment.
  • Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has major plans for AC Milan.

Industry observers note that the RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment. Of course AC Milan will be at the centre of the web, but the idea is to expand.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, the proof of this comes from a three-letter acronym: MSE. It stands for Milan Sports & Entertainment and it is the new holding company created by RedBird. The idea, simply put, is to bring together investments and activities in various sectors under one umbrella.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport recall, Cardinale explained to the Financial Times that the assets involved could be valued in the mid-single-digit billions, meaning several billion dollars. So, how does he plan to get there?

Cardinale linked the creation of MSE to the process initiated with the acquisition of Milan: “Milan Sports & Entertainment is the culmination of this work and of what we have built since we first invested in the club four years ago.”.

In his interview with La Gazzetta, Cardinale clarified that the fresh structure is also created to support the Rossoneri’s sporting ambitions: “The driving force behind operations like this is to provide Milan with the financial strength needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.”.

There are examples of this kind of model working already. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, AEG and Fenway Sports Group are among the most prominent and – given his background in the USA – Cardinale knows each of them well.

According to CNBC valuations, KSE was worth $26.05bn in 2026, FSG $15.37bn, and AEG $11.99bn in 2025, excluding music and hotel businesses.

According to recent reports, KSE boasts franchises such as the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche and Arsenal, as well as venues such as SoFi Stadium, Ball Arena, and Emirates Stadium. The group combines sports, infrastructure and real estate development such as Hollywood Park, the district built around SoFi Stadium.

According to recent reports, AEG – founded by Philip Anschutz – have instead built its model on the management and development of venues. It owns or manages venues such as Crypto.com Arena and The O2 in London plus the Los Angeles Kings and LA Galaxy, and operates in concert promotion and ticketing. The LA LIVE project developed around Crypto.com Arena puts the venue at the centre of a greater ecosystem.

Fenway Sports Group – born around the Boston Red Sox and Liverpool FC – have developed a holding company with interests in media, marketing, real estate, and entertainment. It’s a model Cardinale knows first hand: in 2021, RedBird invested approximately $750m in FSG, acquiring a stake of around 11%, based on an enterprise valuation of $7.35bn.

MSE in theory can harness elements of all three of these experiences: KSE’s integration of sports and infrastructure, AEG ‘s commercial development of facilities and FSG ‘s multi-sport approach. The main difference is the purpose declared by Cardinale: to use all of it to funnel money back into Milan.

From the stadium shared with Inter to the possibility of an arena in San Donato, including the newly introduced NBA Europe venture and even tennis: MSE’s scope includes various initiatives that go beyond the playing field.

Sources indicate that the main infrastructure project is the future Generali Stadium, the newly introduced 71,500-seat facility designed by Foster + Partners and Manica. Developed jointly by the two Milanese clubs, it represents a key element of the transformation of the San Siro area and will not be a Rossoneri-only facility.

The promoters intend for the stadium to host year-round activities, from matches to concerts, as well as catering, events, and hospitality services. In other words, like the stadiums and arenas mentioned above, it will become more than just a place to go for two hours on a Sunday.

In San Donato Milanese, RedBird are also considering the possibility of building a 20,000-seat arena. Cardinale explained that the fund already owns the land and has planning permission, but the idea is also linked to Milan’s potential involvement in NBA Europe. Another area of ​​focus concerns tennis, with the possibility of hosting a tournament in the city.

Finally, RedBird intend to develop a tech giant dedicated to managing stadiums and arenas, with services including catering, merchandising and premium hospitality. The goal is to build commercial expertise to apply to the facilities connected to the group, but also to make it available to other owners and sports clubs.

This phase will be co-ordinated by Brett Yormark, appointed CEO of MSE and set to step down as head of the Big 12 (a conference in College Football) at the end of January 2027. He worked for 14 years at Brooklyn Sports & Entertainment, overseeing the development of the Brooklyn Nets and the Barclays Center. He has also gained experience in NASCAR and Roc Nation.

The choice to go for Yormark reflects the desire to entrust the platform to someone with expertise across multiple different fields in the sporting and commercial worlds.

According to recent reports, all these grand plans are well and good, but how will ideas turn into money that drives AC Milan forward? MSE’s economic potential is measured not only through the club’s revenues, but also through the activities that RedBird intends to develop around sports, infrastructure and entertainment.

It has been revealed that the starting point is obviously Milan as a club, which closed the 2025-26 financial year with revenues of €464.6m, over €100m of which came from sponsorships. The main infrastructure opportunity is the fresh San Siro, an investment of approximately €2.3bn shared with Inter.

Projections contained in the design documents indicate a potential annual revenue of approximately €120.4m for the facility as a whole (both for the Rossoneri and the Nerazzurri), through sporting, commercial, and complementary services.

These are numbers that will be revised upwards by the two clubs when considering, for example, the record agreement with Generali for naming rights. It is worth a total of €650m over 25 years, divided into €10m per year for the first five years and €30m per season for the following 20, once the stadium is built.

One of the areas on which RedBird Capital are focusing most is hospitality, which is presently worth around €15m per year for the Rossoneri. The international benchmark has already been set by Legends Global, a manufacturer Cardinale knows well.

Sources indicate that legends are what the Milan owner sees as a model for developing premium services, restaurants, and commercial spaces. The most obvious example is at FC Barcelona: with the support of LG, the club have marketed nearly 5,000 VIP seats at Camp Nou, generating over €380m in contracted revenue.

It has been revealed that they aim to generate another €700m through multi-year licenses for an additional 2,000 seats. This isn’t annual revenue, but rather contracts spread over 15 or 30 years, so a guaranteed flow of money coming in that Cardinale aims to replicate.

According to recent reports, another agreement which demonstrates the potential of this kind of arrangement is the one with Real Madrid for the Santiago Bernabéu. It involves an investment of approximately €360m in exchange for 20-year participation in some of the stadium’s businesses,.

According to recent reports, legends Global also operate in facilities and events management. Following the acquisition of ASM Global (who actually proposed renovating San Siro for non-football events in Italy) in 2024, the group claims a presence in over 450 venues, approximately 20,000 events, and 165 million guests annually. Their European partnerships include Arsenal, Chelsea and Porto.

FC Barcelona debuts new VIP seating licenses at Spotify Camp Nou with Legends Global.

🔗 More details: https://t.co/awtEsnYE6X pic.twitter.com/iCMuM0QD35.

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 25, 2026.

To illustrate the potential it could hold for Italy as a whole, the English subsidiary reported revenues of £131.6m in 2024, of which £105.5m came from facility and event management and £26.1m from catering. Before the integration with ASM Global, Legends had reported revenues of $1.7bn in the period ending in March 2024, with 67% coming from food and beverage sales.

Industry observers note that in Italy, a benchmark is Forumnet, who in 2024 generated €29.7m in revenue and €12.8m in EBITDA (Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation). They manage the Assago Forum which hosts approximately 60-70 concerts a year, demonstrating how a venue can generate activity well beyond the sports calendar.

In a recent development, as mentioned, an arena is being planned in San Donato with an estimated investment of around €400m, which could become the basis for a Milanese franchise in NBA Europe. For reference, Olimpia Milano – the current basketball team in the city – generate around €15m through ticketing, season tickets, sponsorships and merchandising.

For NBA Europe, projections speak of over $1.5bn to be distributed to the clubs in the first six years. A theoretical division among the 12 permanent franchises would equate to approximately $20.8m per team per year, but this is not fixed yet. Entry costs – estimated by the media to be between $500m and over $1bn – also remain to be determined.

Tennis represents another potential area for development. The ATP 500 in Halle generates around €5m in revenue, excluding television rights, while the ATP Finals in Turin generate around €60m. These are events with different dimensions and scopes, but they provide a scale.

The creation of MSE has a stated objective: to strengthen Milan’s financial capacity and reduce the gap with the richest clubs on the international scene, particularly those in the Premier League.

The gap is also evident when comparing revenues. AC Milan closed the 2025-26 season with €464.6m, a significant result considering their absence from European competitions , but still far from the top English clubs.

According to the Deloitte Football Money League, in the 2024-25 season, Liverpool generated €836.1m, Arsenal €821.7m and Manchester United €793.1m. Tottenham and Chelsea also exceeded €670m and €580m, respectively.

In a recent development, the comparison covers different financial years, but it still shows the magnitude of the gap. Liverpool generated revenues equal to approximately 1.8 times those of Milan, while Chelsea recorded a turnover approximately €120 higher.

In a recent development, the chasm shows how clubs in the Premier League have showcased an ability to generate commercial revenue, enhance stadiums and reach a global audience. The gap has only been growing, and TV rights will be another focus, though that is outside of just Cardinale’s hands.

Industry observers note that speaking of the owner, it is now obvious he sees MSE as the name that will house the tools to try build a real sporting and commercial world around Milan. It remains to be seen how effective it will be, but the starting point is there.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham’s veteran midfielder has been the subject of an honest interview in his home country on Czech radio coinciding with the release of his autobiography. One of the more revealing comments Tomas Soucek made concerns the pressure and the expectation of playing in front of a massive audience – such as West Ham will undoubtedly face tomorrow as the season re-commences with a home tie at London Stadium in front of 60,000 expectant supporters.

Unlike several others, from his words it is clear that Soucek seems to thrive on the pressure and the weight of expectation upon him. As one of only a handful of medal winners still at the club from the 2023 campaign, Soucek’s experience should become a steadying influence in the dressing room even though he mostly starts games on the bench these days.

Handling the weight of expectation at London Stadium has been daunting at times.

‘Tornado Tom’ reveals that, far from letting it get to him, he actually enjoys the weight of expectation and pressure :.

It has been revealed that “Yes, obviously I feel it, but I like the pressure. Because football is always up and down, you have so many wins and so many losses – and it’s up to you how you recover from all of it.

“And I love that. As you remarked, it’s the most watched league in the world. And West Ham’s fans are crazy – they’re the best in the league, and it’s such a historic club.

“From the first day until now, I think me and West Ham connection is as good as it could possibly be in all aspects.

“And, yes, the pressure is there, but I try to work with it – and that’s why we play football.” (englishradio.cz).

Sources indicate that the pressure will be significantly eased with a clean sheet and three points tomorrow – whether Soucek now, 31 gets into the action or simply acts as a calming figure in the dressing room. He is one of those very rare characters in the West Ham team – a leader on and off the pitch – and in another era could have spent years as the club’s captain.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham’s rejuvenated striker Joel Piroe, fresh from a successful international break with Suriname, could hardly have picked a better opponent to face as West Ham prepare to resume their Championship campaign against Preston North End tomorrow and the Hammers’ on-loan striker seeks a return to front line duties under fresh boss Scott Parker.

Piroe hasn’t featured regularly under Nuno and he will be hoping for a change of fortunes under the Hammers’ latest head coach: The Dutch-born Suriname striker has something of a happy history against Saturday’s visitors, having scored four goals in eight previous appearances against the Lilywhites.

Proving he’s bang in form, Piroe’s two goals for Suriname last week will surely give Scott Parker the nudge needed to promoting him ahead of Taty Castellanos into the starting eleven.

The former Leeds striker has demonstrated his ability to find the net in the Championship, unlike West Ham’s often-moody Argentine forward who has but one goal to his name this season in what can only be seen as a massive disappointment.

For a side desperate to build some momentum, a striker returning from international duty with two goals under his belt and a proven record against tomorrow’s opponents can’t be overlooked.

Opportunity knocks – if Piroe can extend his Preston scoring record tomorrow he could cement a place in the starting eleven for the rest of the year. Most fans – me included – have lost patience with Taty Castellanos who doesn’t seem inclined to influence games – time for Piroe to show what he can do in an extended run in the team.

Emotional Mauricio Pochettino gets perfect sendoff in his US farewell... before boarding jet for latest life as Manchester United manager

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1398 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 21:06 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 00:56 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino received a near-perfect sendoff as US men's national team head coach on Tuesday in Cincinnati, where Manchester United's next manager watched his now-former players beat Haiti before bidding an emotional farewell to his adopted country.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:06 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 00:56 EST, 18 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino received a near-perfect sendoff as US men's national team head coach on Tuesday in Cincinnati, where Manchester United's next manager watched his now-former players beat Haiti before bidding an emotional farewell to his adopted country.

Christian Pulisic, Pochettino's brightest pupil over the last two seasons, rose to the occasion by scoring on a gravity-defying bicycle kick in the 25th minute and 18-year-old prospect Julian Hall followed in the 43rd with a goal of his own.

But for all of the excitement on the field – where Pochettino helped rebuild the American attack with a high-intensity style – all eyes were on the manager as he embraced his team one last time.

Recent findings suggest that with the 2-0 win (8-0 aggregate), the USMNT now advances to the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, but that's no longer Pochettino's concern. Instead, former American fullback and current under-23 manager Steve Cherundolo is expected to take over on an interim basis, while Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one win in the English Premier League through 10 matches this season.

Industry observers note that 'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino mentioned after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'.

Following the win, Pochettino was scheduled to fly from northern Kentucky to Manchester aboard a private plane chartered by his fresh club. The quick escape offered the chance to avoid major airlines following Friday's chaotic nationwide shutdown, and perhaps a few hours' sleep for a 54-year-old starting his new job on Wednesday at Carrington Training Centre.

Pochettino spent two years with the USMNT, helping to rebuild an attack around Pulisic.

Pochettino hugs a staff member prior to the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match.

Pochettino paces along a near-empty sideline after much of his staff left for Manchester.

And Pochettino didn't plan on traveling alone.

Outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott were expected to join Pochettino aboard the flight to Manchester, where assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

According to recent reports, the quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

The Argentine national is replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

In a recent development, 'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'.

Mauricio Pochettino saying his final goodbyes to the USA fans as he's now gonna fly to Manchester immediately ❤️ pic.twitter.com/sCe8LCjpK5.

Pulisic, perhaps Pochettino's brightest pupil, scored on a bicycle kick in the 25th minute.

Pulisic celebrates his goal on Tuesday night in Cincinnati during the win over Haiti.

Pochettino was expected to board a flight from northern Kentucky to Manchester after the win.

Pochettino had been on something of a farewell tour in the US, where he embraced the local sports scene over his brief tenure. In between overseeing his final games with the USMNT, Pochettino was spotted at the Cincinnati Bengals' win over the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

The manager, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead before kickoff, where he mingled with Bengals special teamers such as kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow.

A night earlier, Pochettino guided the US to a 6-0 win over Haiti in Miami to give his team a safe cushion for his farewell on Tuesday in Cincinnati.

Pochettino broke down in tears as he announced his decision last week, while admitting he couldn't turn down the 'dream' job with Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino walks on the field after the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal.

American fans give Pochettino a standing ovation in Cincinnati after his farewell match.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team's headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

Recent findings suggest that 'I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,' he said. 'It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

'I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

'Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

'In some part it's a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

United will pay the US Soccer Federation more than $13.2 million (£10m) in compensation for Pochettino and his backroom staff.

According to recent reports, 'I never mentioned I wanted to go back in the Premier League,' Pochettino, a former Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton boss, told reporters last week. 'All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear.'.

Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one EPL win.

Mauricio Pochettino insisted it was the 'most difficult decision' to leave the USMNT.

Pochettino put together a 23-12-2 record with the US, while 78 players earned caps for the US over his tenure. Remarkably, nine teenagers made their USMNT debuts for Pochettino, including Hall, who scored on Tuesday.

In a recent development, but the Americans failed to crack into the sport's upper echelon during Pochettino's brief tenure in the US. In his lone World Cup appearance with the team last summer, Pochettino guided the USMNT to the Round of 16, where the Americans fell to Belgium, 4-1.

That result was an improvement on 2018, when the US failed to qualify, but not on 2022, when then-coach Gregg Berhalter's similarly team fell short of the quarters with a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands.

Despite this, Pochettino's American players have remained largely supportive of his tenure, including Berhalter's son Sebastian, who remarked the outgoing coach helped him 'develop as a player and as a person.'.

Prior to Tuesday's win, Pochettino thanked American fans for the support he received over his two years with the national team.

Sources indicate that 'Thank you so much from the bottom of my heart for all the fans, for all the people that was supporting us in the last two years,' Pochettino said in a video posted on social media. 'Special, great memories of the World Cup and everything that we lived together. Always in my heart, always one of you. All the best and I wish everything good for the future.'.

Potential candidates to replace Pochettino in the US include former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, ex-England manager Gareth Southgate and some lesser-known candidates like Cherundolo, who now guides the United States U-23 team.

'For us to win, we need to be great at a lot of things, and we need someone who cares about youth development, cares about our youth national team programs, our relationships with our clubs and the success of the federation more broadly,' US Soccer CEO JT Batson told TNT Sports on Tuesday. 'We know that is a key part of our success, and it's also a key part of how we've been able to attract great people because they get to do significant things.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:48.
  • On their return to league action after a weekend off for the international break, Luton Town will head to the Pirelli Stadium to take on Burton Albion on Saturday.
  • The visitors sit five points outside of the top two in the League One table in the midst of a seven-game unbeaten streak in all competitions while their hosts are 15th after consecutive league defeats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:48.

On their return to league action after a weekend off for the international break, Luton Town will head to the Pirelli Stadium to take on Burton Albion on Saturday.

The visitors sit five points outside of the top two in the League One table in the midst of a seven-game unbeaten streak in all competitions while their hosts are 15th after consecutive league defeats.

Burton Albion head into the weekend aiming to bounce back from a pair of defeats and move back towards the top half of League One.

Aiming to build on a 17th-placed finish last time around, the Brewers enjoyed a positive start to the newly introduced term, earning 17 points from their first 13 outings courtesy of four wins, five draws and four defeats.

That was largely thanks to a solid home record, having only lost once in seven league outings at the Pirelli Stadium, most recently beating Leyton Orient 2-1, only to suffer consecutive away losses in their last two third-tier games.

A trip to Wycombe Wanderers ended in a 2-0 loss, before they followed up consecutive cup matches with a visit to MK Dons and suffered a 6-2 beating, having fallen 3-0 and 6-1 behind with goals from Emeka Adiele and Kain Adom nothing more than consolations.

Now sat 15th, but just two points off 11th-placed Leicester City, Burton Albion will bid to put those league defeats behind them and bounce back to winning ways at the Pirelli Stadium.

They face another tough test, though, as the visitors arrive aiming to continue an unbeaten run and narrow their gap to the league leaders.

In their first full season under Jack Wilshere, after falling agonisingly short in their playoff pursuit under him late last season, Luton Town currently sit fourth with 24 points on the board from 14 games.

The Hatters lost four of their first nine league games but have since bounced back in style, rebounding from the last of those with four straight wins over Barnsley, Leicester City, Doncaster Rovers and Peterborough United.

A trip to league leaders Huddersfield Town then followed, and Wilshere's men left with a creditable point from a 1-1 draw having led through Jordan Clark and been pegged back by Joe Taylor, before they hosted Forest Green Rovers in the FA Cup first round before the international break and won 2-0 with Emilio Lawrence and Clark on the scoresheet.

Now on the back of a free weekend last time out due to international call-ups, and a 3-0 EFL Trophy win over Peterborough United on Tuesday as Clark again scored alongside Nahki Wells and Devante Cole, Luton Town turn their focus back to League One and will hope to narrow their five-point gap to the top two with a fifth win in six league matches on Saturday.

Burton Albion form (all competitions):.

Luton Town form (all competitions):.

Burton Albion are set to remain without Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers on Saturday due to injuries.

Matthew Dennis also missed their last game, and in his and Vickers's expected absence, Mark O'Mahony should again lead the line for the Brewers.

He should again have support from star man Charlie Webster and Kain Adom who scored against MK Dons last time out, while Kegs Chauke is a mainstay in midifeld.

Luton Town are still unable to call on the injured trio of Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris, who is yet to feature this season.

Wilshere fielded a strong starting XI for their midweek EFL Trophy tie with Peterborough and the Hatters will look similar on Saturday, with Wells continuing to lead the line having netted his ninth goal of the season in that win.

He will have support from Kasey Palmer and Jordan Clark, who also scored last time out to make it a goal in each of his last four games, while Dan Gore will hope to continue alongside midfield mainstay Liam Walsh despite Wilshere often fielding another attacking midfielder in League One action.

Burton Albion possible starting lineup:.

Addai; Araujo, Tilt, Sibbick; Borges Rodrigues, Chauke, Krubally, Adiele; Webster, O'Mahony, Adom.

Luton Town possible starting lineup:.

Shea; Jones, Andersen, Johnston, Ashby; Walsh; Richards, Clark, Donley, Palmer; Wells.

Burton Albion have seen their resilient start to the season halted in recent weeks, and we see them falling short against a strong Luton team who have won six of their last seven matches in all competitions.

#37983. All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 29m • 📚 Deep Dive (5895 w)
