Recent findings suggest that figure 5c,d shows the band dispersions along the \(\overline{\Gamma }-\overline{{\rm{Z}}}\) direction measured in domains A and B using right-handed and left-handed polarized light. Under circularly right-polarized illumination, FB1 and FB3 exhibit stronger spectral weight than FB2 in one domain and weaker spectral weight in the other, generating a clear domain contrast (Fig. 5c). Reversing the light polarization from circularly right-polarized to circularly left-polarized reverses this contrast, producing opposite circular-dichroism signals in domains A and B (Fig. 5e). The circular dichroism is associated with the orbital angular momentum of the Eu 4f bands with b-axis net moment25,26 (Fig. 5f and Supplementary Note 11). The calculated orbital angular momentum reverses between opposite magnetic chiralities, consistent with the observed reversal of the circular-dichroism signal. Thus, the micro-ARPES measurements reveal domains with opposite magnetic chirality and opposite b-axis moment.

Industry observers note that the temperature-dependent spatial maps in Fig. 5g show that the domain contrast persists in the conical magnetic phase, weakens in the spiral magnetic phase above TN2 and disappears in the paramagnetic phase. In contrast, MFM no longer resolves the domains in the spiral magnetic phase because of the absence of a net magnetic moment detectable by this probe. The remaining circular-dichroism contrast in the spiral magnetic phase may originate from domains with different chirality, although its microscopic origin requires further scrutiny. Overall, the domain-dependent circular-dichroism demonstrates the coupling between magnetic chirality and the electronic structure. Reversing the magnetic chirality therefore reverses the circular-dichroism response of the electronic states, providing a means to probe the chirality-dependent electronic structure associated with the p-wave magnetic state.

We now discuss the similarities and differences between p-wave magnetic spin splitting and the previously studied f-wave11 spin splitting in transition-metal dichalcogenides. Previous theoretical and experimental studies have demonstrated that in monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (for example, MoS2), SOC induces odd-parity spin splitting in the valence bands27,28,29. Because this splitting is of relativistic origin in a non-magnetic crystal, it is relatively weak and cannot be easily tuned30. By contrast, first-principles calculations predict p-wave spin splitting in EuSi arising predominantly from non-relativistic exchange, whereas ARPES reveals a substantial magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure (Supplementary Table 6). Because this p-wave state originates from the chiral magnetic order, the calculated dependence of the spin texture on magnetic chirality suggests a possible route to controlling the associated spin polarization.

It has been revealed that compared with previously discussed ‘p-wave’ magnetic candidates8,9, EuSi provides a particularly clean realization of the archetypal p-wave symmetry setting8. In the spiral phase, the refined magnetic structure of stoichiometric EuSi preserves the combined \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) symmetry and has zero net magnetization, providing the symmetry setting for the predicted odd-parity p-wave spin texture without complications from finite magnetization. This combination has not been achieved in earlier candidate materials such as NiI2 or Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12. In NiI2, \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) symmetry is broken by the incommensurate non-collinear spin structure8, whereas in Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12 a weak magnetization breaks time-reversal symmetry and generates a large anomalous Hall effect9.

In a recent development, furthermore, EuSi serves as an advantageous material platform because of its stoichiometric and metallic nature, and a relatively high temperature window (33.4–62 K) compared with those of low-ordering-temperature metallic counterparts such as CeNiAsO and Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12 (approximately 8 K; see Supplementary Table 7 for detailed comparison). Taken together, these attributes position EuSi as a particularly promising material platform for exploring and ultimately harnessing p-wave magnetism in electronic structures.

Recent findings suggest that metallic p-wave magnets are predicted to host unconventional responses, including field-free spin-polarized transport, a large non-relativistic Edelstein effect10 and non-relativistic Ising superconductivity11. When the spiral order is canted and forms a conical state, an unconventional and large anomalous Hall effect can be observed. Analogous effects, such as the magneto-optical Kerr effect, are expected to be pronounced as well. Through combined theoretical and experimental approaches, our results provide evidence for p-wave magnetism in the electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, associated with its chiral magnetic order and combined time-reversal and lattice-translation symmetry in the spiral phase (33.4–62 K). EuSi therefore provides a realistic and accessible platform for investigating symmetry-protected transport and optical responses driven by magnetism. Beyond fundamental interest, the controllability of its metallic and chiral magnetic states may enable field-free spintronic functionalities and pave the way towards engineering p-wave-correlated and topological electronic phases in itinerant systems.

EuSi single crystals were grown using the Bridgman method with an Eu:Si elemental ratio of 1:1. Eu (99.95% purity) and Si (99.99% purity) were mixed and placed in a tantalum crucible. The crucible was sealed in vacuum. The sealed tube was heated to 1,450 °C for over 12 h and maintained at that temperature for 24 h. The solution was then slowly cooled to room temperature. Owing to the sensitivity of the investigated phase to oxygen and moisture, the specimen used for the single-crystal diffraction experiment was prepared (mounted) in a protective atmosphere (an argon-filled glovebox). The single crystal used for this experiment was mechanically detached (cut) from the grown single crystal and mounted in a glass capillary (0.2 mm diameter) to prevent reaction with air and moisture during the data collection. Details regarding data collection and the refinement of the crystal structure are listed in the Supplementary Tables 1–3. Low-temperature X-ray powder diffraction was carried out at beamline ID22 of the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF). For this purpose, a portion of the grown single crystal was powdered, sieved through a 32-µm sieve and placed into a 0.3-mm glass capillary. The data were collected at specific temperatures using a helium-cooled cryostat and a multi-analyser stage for recording of the diffraction pattern. At temperatures below 45 K, the intensity of the beam was reduced using an attenuator to prevent the sample from heating up. The results of the low-temperature X-ray powder diffraction are shown in Supplementary Fig. 4.

Recent findings suggest that X-ray absorption spectroscopy and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism measurements were performed at the high-field magnet endstation of beamline I10 at Diamond Light Source, UK, with a base temperature of 5 K and magnetic field up to ±14 T along the direction of the incident beam. The crystals were cleaved in situ along the a–c (010) plane under ultrahigh vacuum, and the angle between the incident beam and the crystal (010) plane was kept at either 0° (normal incidence) or 70° (grazing incidence). X-ray absorption spectroscopy was carried out in total-electron-yield mode at the Eu M4,5 edges. X-ray magnetic circular-dichroism spectra were obtained by subtracting the absorption spectra measured with opposite helicities of the incident X-ray beam, which was aligned either parallel or antiparallel to the applied magnetic field.

High-resolution ARPES measurements were performed at beamlines BL5-2 of the Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource (SSRL), A-branch of the Bloch beamline at MAX IV, and BL03U of the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility (SSRF). At BL5-2, a Scienta Omicron DFS30 analyser was used, achieving an overall energy and angular resolution of 20 meV and 0.2°. At Bloch and BL03U, a Scienta Omicron DA30L analyser was used, achieving an overall energy and angular resolution of 20 meV and 0.2°. High-resolution laser-based ARPES measurements were performed on home-built set-up (hν = 6.994 eV) at ShanghaiTech University. Data were collected using an electron analyser (DA30L Scienta Omicron). The total convolved energy and angle resolution were 5 meV and 0.1°, respectively. Micro-ARPES measurements were performed at BL07U of SSRF. The beam with photon energy from 88 eV to 102 eV was focused using a Fresnel zone plate and a spatial resolution of approximately 400 nm was achieved. The data were collected by a hemispherical Scienta Omicron DA30L electron analyser. The instrument energy and momentum resolution were approximately 15 meV and 0.01 Å−1, respectively. In all set-ups, the samples were cleaved in situ at approximately 10 K and measured under ultrahigh vacuum below 5 × 10−11 torr.

Recent findings suggest that the spin-resolved ARPES experiments were performed using a Scienta DA30L analyser integrated with a very-low-energy-diffraction spin detector at the National Synchrotron Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) BL13U. The samples were cleaved in situ at approximately 40 K and measured under ultrahigh vacuum below 2 × 10−10 torr. For these experiments, an effective Sherman function of 0.25 was used. Spin-resolved ARPES measurements at the U125-PGM beamline of BESSY II were performed using the spin-ARPES endstation equipped with a Scienta R4000 analyser coupled to two Mott-type spin detectors. The samples were also cleaved in situ at approximately 50 K and measured under ultrahigh vacuum below 2 × 10−10 torr. For these experiments, an effective Sherman function of 0.16 was adopted. The spin polarization was determined from \(\mathrm{Polarization}=(1/{S}_{\mathrm{eff}})\times ({I}_{\mathrm{up}}-{I}_{\mathrm{down}})/({I}_{\mathrm{up}}+{I}_{\mathrm{down}})\), in which Iup and Idown are the measured photoelectron intensities in the two spin channels and Seff is the effective Sherman function.

Sources indicate that the statistical uncertainties were estimated from the counting statistics of the two spin-detector channels. Assuming independent Poisson statistics, the measured counts Iup and Idown have standard deviations \({\sigma }_{{I}_{\mathrm{up}}}=\sqrt{{I}_{\mathrm{up}}}\) and \({\sigma }_{{I}_{\mathrm{down}}}=\sqrt{{I}_{\mathrm{down}}}\), respectively. Standard error propagation gives \({\sigma }_{{S}_{y}}=\frac{2}{{S}_{\mathrm{eff}}}\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{\mathrm{up}}{I}_{\mathrm{down}}}{{({I}_{\mathrm{up}}+{I}_{\mathrm{down}})}^{3}}}\). For energy-dependent polarization curves, this expression was applied separately to each energy bin; for the integrated polarization of a spectral feature, Iup and Idown represent the total counts accumulated within the corresponding energy-integration window. All shaded uncertainty envelopes and error bars in the spin-ARPES figures denote one standard deviation.

Industry observers note that neutron-diffraction experiments were conducted at the HB-3A DEMAND in the High-Flux Isotope Reactor at Oak Ridge National Lab. A piece of a EuSi single crystal with dimensions of approximately 4 × 3 × 0.1 mm3 was aligned in the (0KL) scattering plane and cooled. The wavelength used was 1.541 Å. The data were reduced using MANTID31 and ReTIA32. Symmetry analysis was performed using SARAh33, and magnetic-structure refinement was performed using FullProf34,35.

The first-principles calculations of the band structures and Fermi surface were performed by using the first-principles DFT methods implemented in the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP)36,37. The exchange-correlation and the ion-electron interactions are treated by the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof functional38 and the projector augmented-wave method39,40 under the generalized gradient approximation. Throughout all calculations, the convergence criteria for energy are less than 2 × 10−5 eV, and the plane-wave energy cut-off is set to 400 eV. The k-point sampling uses a Monkhorst–Pack scheme41 with an accuracy of 0.02π Å−1 for self-consistent electronic calculations. To correctly describe the strong correlation effects of the Eu f orbitals, the on-site Coulomb interaction was treated using an effective Hubbard U of 5 eV.

For electrical-transport measurements, a single crystal was cut into a bar shape. A standard six-probe method was used for longitudinal resistivity and transverse Hall measurements. Electrical-transport data were collected using a physical-property measurement system (PPMS; Quantum Design). Magnetic-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements were performed using a magnetic property measurement system (MPMS; Quantum Design) and PPMS. Thermal-expansion measurements were conducted in the PPMS using a homemade capacitive dilatometer.

In a recent development, the MFM experiments were performed with a homemade helium-3 atomic force microscopy system using commercial piezoresistive cantilevers (spring constant k ≈ 3 N m−1 and resonant frequency approximately 43 kHz). The tips were coated with a nominally 100-nm-thick cobalt layer by magnetron sputtering. The MFM data were acquired by Nanonis SPM Controllers (SPECS) with a phase-locked loop. The MFM signal, the resonant frequency shift of the cantilever, is proportional to the out-of-plane stray field gradient generated by the sample. By using the constant-height mode, MFM images are acquired on a scanning plane approximately 200 nm above the surface.

Former Manchester United and Chelsea star Juan Mata has retired from football at the age of 38.

The Spain star, who came through Real Madrid's academy before winning the Champions League with Chelsea and the Europa League with both the Blues and Man United, enjoyed a dazzling career in England before moving to clubs in Turkey, Japan and Australia.

The midfielder also distinguished himself for his national side, winning the 2010 World Cup as part of the squad, and scoring in Spain's victorious Euro 2012 final against Italy.

Most recently featuring in Australia's A-League for Melbourne Victory, Mata unveiled the end of his playing career with a poignant video filmed inside a dressing room to the sound of Elvis Presley's 'Now or Never'.

In the clip, Mata symbolically hangs his boots on a hook in the locker room before leaving, with the video captioned: 'Sometimes, to love is to let go.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes, to love… is to let go. THANKS FOOTBALL. ⚽️❤️♾️A veces, amar… es dejar ir. GRACIAS FÚTBOL. ⚽️❤️♾️ pic.twitter.com/v7otd6AyOq.

Juan Mata has revealed his retirement from football with a poignant video message (Source: Juan Mata).

The former Chelsea and Man United midfielder enjoyed a decorated career on English soil.

A popular presence wherever he plied his trade, Mata's comments on social media were soon flooded with well-wishes from former clubs.

'Great player, better person,' Man United shared under his post on X. 'Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan (red heart emoji).'.

Chelsea had a similar send-off for him, with the club writing: 'So many special memories. Thank you, Juan (blue heart emoji).'.

Former Chelsea executive Marina Granovskaia added her personal thanks with a message too, writing: 'Great video! Great career too! (red heart emoji). Wishing you all the best Juan (blue heart emoji).'.

Former team-mates including Ander Herrera, Ashley Young, Santi Cazorla and Mario Suarez were among those to send messages of thanks and congratulations, with Man City star Vivianne Miedema also writing to Mata.

'Congratulations on an amazing career and changing football on and off the pitch (hand clap emoji, green heart emoji),' the Dutch WSL trailblazer wrote.

Despite starting his youth career at Real Madrid, Mata's first senior minutes in the Spanish top flight came with his move in 2007 to Valencia.

Mata notched up 174 appearances for the side and won the Copa del Rey in club colours before his landmark move to Chelsea.

In west London, the midfielder won the FA Cup and Champions League in his first season, and the Europa League in his second.

The video contained a brief farewell message and was widely liked by his former team-mates.

After leaving Chelsea, the Spaniard enjoyed a strong stint at Manchester United.

At the end of last month, the Euro 2012 winner was treated to a lap of appreciation at his last club Melbourne Victory.

But a falling-out with then-coach Jose Mourinho called time on his stint at Stamford Bridge and a move north to join Man United – where he would later reunite with the Portuguese manager during his stint in Manchester between 2016 and 2018.

Mata later enjoyed stints at Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before his move to Melbourne.

In recent years, however, Mata has expanded his career away from the pitch, with the player serving as a pundit at this year's World Cup for ITV, and at the 2024 European Championship for BBC Sport.

As well as appearing in the media, Mata is a keen investor in sporting ventures including Spanish club Real Oviedo, San Diego FC in the MLS and Formula One's Alpine racing team.

Alongside Italy icon Giorgio Chiellini, Mata is an investor in Mercury/13, a women's multi-club ownership group that invests in FC Como Women.

Mata is also a co-owner of Melbourne Victory, with plans to chair a football committee at the club after hanging up his boots.

As well as a shrewd businessman, Mata is also a philanthropist – and was recognised for his donations with an MBE in June 2025.

In 2017, Mata pledged one per cent of his salary to a charitable movement called Common Goal, which supports football charities.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 02:21.

Brighton & Hove Albion owner Tony Bloom has claimed that Fabian Hurzeler supports Bayern Munich and could move there in the future.

The Seagulls have been the surprise package of the Premier League season, with the club currently in second place after 10 matchweeks.

Few could have predicted that they would also be the division's top scorers (26), and the team's form has led to universal praise for boss Hurzeler.

The German head coach has understandably been linked with a number of sides in the league, including Manchester United, though the Red Devils have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as Michael Carrick's replacement.

Industry observers note that speaking to reporters, Brighton owner Bloom insisted that he intends to keep Hurzeler at the club for a long time, though admitted that Bayern Munich could tempt the manager, saying: "Fabian is doing an unbelievable job. He is really enjoying it here and we would fight ridiculously hard to keep him if we had to.

It has been revealed that "I don’t think he is going anywhere for a long time and we are just enjoying the ride. He is improving. We have given him the facilities, the players, the set-up to really grow as a head coach and he is taking that opportunity. We are very fortunate to have him and long may that continue.

"He will be at the top or near the top of the [list for the] best clubs in the world when they need to hire, but he’s young. He can go to these major clubs down the road [time-wise]. [Bayern Munich] is his team. I am sure he will be head coach of Bayern Munich at some time probably.".

Brighton are in a much stronger position than 18th-placed United, so it would make sense if Hurzeler was reluctant about potentially joining them in favour of a more stable team Bayern.

While Hurzeler may be the brightest prospect in management, Premier League clubs may find it difficult to appoint him in the coming years.

United have only just appointed Pochettino, so they will almost certainly spend considerable time and resources on the Argentine.

Arsenal are likely to keep Mikel Arteta for a number of seasons, while Manchester City could be demoted to lower divisions.

Liverpool are embarking upon their first campaign under Andoni Iraola, and it would be extraordinary if they sacked him after one season.

Chelsea have never been afraid to sack a head coach, so Xabi Alonso's position should not necessarily be seen as secure, but the Spaniard is highly regarded by many.

Given Bayern Munich right now employ Vincent Kompany, the Bavarians may not be in the market for a new head coach for a considerable period.

That could have left an opening for United to approach Brighton for Hurzeler, though it is far too early to suggest that the Red Devils have made a mistake by not trying to appoint the 33-year-old.

The club are in the relegation zone, and convincing Brighton to part with Hurzeler may have been impossible, especially as the Seagulls could realistically qualify for the Champions League.

Hiring an interim boss could have deepened United's relegation woes, and of the managers available in November, there were few with the pedigree of Pochettino.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paolo Scaroni has insisted that AC Milan have a long-term project under Gerry Cardinale, for which the stadium is a vital component.

As we wrote about at length last night, Cardinale has big intends to help get Milan back towards the top end of European football. The new ‘MSE’ holding organization is the latest development, while the Generali Stadium was recently unveiled, and other projects like the NBA Europe team are ongoing.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is all part of a mission to try and make the Rossoneri brand more than just a football club. Scaroni has been the face of the stadium project for many years, and he was a guest at a sports talk organised by RCS and entitled ‘Attracting foreign capital and enhancing the system for a real relaunch’.

He spoke alongside Giovanni Carnevali (CEO and General Manager of Juventus), Giuseppe Marotta (President and CEO of Inter) and Ezio Maria Simonelli, (President of the Lega Calcio Serie A). His words are via MilanNews.

Industry observers note that serie A seems to be struggling compared to other Italian sports. What could be done to make football more competitive?

Industry observers note that “You’re telling me about something we’re doing, Gerry Cardinale’s idea. He came to the world of Italian football after twenty-five years in sport.

“It’s about creating Milan Sport Entertainment, that is, creating other sports around Milan, combining other sports with football, providing entertainment, communicating, and using Milan and Milano – because he also places great importance on the city of Milan, which is one of Europe’s emerging cities – to create an attractive environment for other sports and other situations.

“I’ll give just one example: if you take the United States, which is a gigantic market for the world of sports, football comes in fifth among the sports that Americans love, after basketball, of course, and even after hockey.

It has been revealed that “So, how do we make football – and, in our case, Serie A – attractive in the United States? Precisely by creating this concept of entertainment around football, this concept of Milan, of fashion, of spectacle, that is, creating an attractiveness that competes with the other sports we compete with every day.

According to recent reports, “This is the idea that Gerry brought in Italy, coming from his vast experience in the world of sport, and therefore around this we look to our future. Gerry Cardinale comes to say that he will never sell Milan, precisely because his project is a long-term one.”.

The Generali Stadium will be something more than a stadium and will help this….

It has been revealed that “Let’s say it’s been quite a complex journey. A very long one that I’ve been on with Inter since 2018-2019. But we’ve reached, let’s say, some key milestones. The first was in November last year, when we bought the San Siro stadium.

“The Meazza belongs to Inter and Milan, and the entire surrounding area. So every now and then I read debates: ‘But should it be torn down, shouldn’t it be torn down?’. Well, this will be a decision we’ll make because it’s ours, so I want to say: we have a clear, notarial fact behind us that gives us ownership of the San Siro stadium.

“This was the first step. The second was the presentation of the stadium that we held a few weeks ago. I think the Milanese and the professionals liked this presentation of this stadium designed by two great architects: one who worked on the exterior of the stadium and another who was responsible for the division of the spaces inside.

“Building a great stadium like this is something extremely crucial. Technical. Because then, as always when you tackle new topics, you learn things. I, for example, learned that Manica – this organization that designs our stadium – has built six hundred stadiums around the world.

Industry observers note that “So, to say that building a stadium is a profession, it’s not something you improvise. And this was the second step. The third was that Generali seized the opportunity to own this fresh stadium and the old one as well, because the collaboration on the Generali Stadium begins now.

“They seized the opportunity to have the two great Milanese clubs in Milan, both of which have a history of victories, are known worldwide and have millions of fans worldwide, and to use this new stadium to promote their image, I would say especially in Europe – because Generali are a very European company – but I would also say worldwide.

According to recent reports, “They seized a great opportunity because opportunities like this are just the ones you get. And so I must say the negotiations concluded very successfully.”.

“We have all the authorisations in front of us by September 2027. Therefore, in principle, we could begin construction of the new stadium between the end of 2027 and the beginning of 2028. So, let’s say, we’re pretty close to the home stretch.

“Naturally, as always with these issues, there may be some discussion points. Furthermore, in Milan we’re heading towards an election campaign for a newly introduced mayor, and a topic like the construction of a new stadium is one that can naturally excite politicians.

“Let’s say we’re confident because the entire process we’ve taken so far protects us from these potential disruptions, and we’re fiercely determined to move forward. With the upcoming stadium, among other things, we’ll have €100 million in additional revenue.

“This €100 million in additional revenue is a fundamental ingredient for the success of AC Milan, Inter Milan, and Serie A around the world, because ultimately, €100 million – to have great players, to pay great players – is a fundamental ingredient for success.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 02:51, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 05:04.

Hoping to solidify their spot in the top half of the Scottish Premiership, Dundee United will travel to face Hibernian at Easter Road Stadium.

The Hibees are keen to pick up where they left off with a win, while the Tangerines could make it eight games unbeaten.

Marink Reedijk's Hibs have endured a difficult campaign to date, and fans will be looking to see a rejuvenated team emerge on their return from the international break.

The Hibees went winless throughout the entirety of October, and by the end of the month had racked up a total of six matches without a victory, losing four times in the process.

However, Reedijk's side came from behind to beat Hearts 2-1 in the Scottish League Cup semi-final on November 1, courtesy of goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath.

That Edinburgh Derby success may have marked a turning point for Hibs, who went on to thrash Aberdeen 4-0 in the Scottish Premiership six days later, McGrath once again decisive as he netted the opener early in the second half.

Earning a first league win since August 30 has left the Hibees 10th in the table with 11 points after 12 games, from where they could climb up to eighth given that Motherwell and St Mirren are set to play Rangers and Celtic respectively this weekend.

On the other hand, Reedijk's men remain just two points above bottom-of-the-table Kilmarnock, and with five defeats to go with a single draw from their six most recent home clashes, it would take a shock for the hosts to prevail on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Jim Goodwin's Dundee Utd have their sights set on cementing their place in the top six, and this weekend's trip to Easter Road could be crucial.

The Tangerines are at the moment sixth with 17 points, level with city rivals Dundee in fifth and just three points behind fourth-placed Hearts.

That being noted, Goodwin's side will be looking over their shoulder at seventh-placed St Johnstone - who they are also level on points with - and eighth-placed St Mirren, who are just three points behind.

Considering that Saturday's result may be directionally significant for Dundee Utd, fans will take heart from the fact the team arrive on the back of a seven-game unbeaten streak after their 1-1 draw with Motherwell on November 7, not to mention that the Tangerines have lost just one of their last five away clashes.

However, it is notable that the visitors' undefeated run features four draws alongside three wins, and it remains to be seen whether they can secure maximum points against a potentially resurgent Hibs on home turf.

Dundee United Scottish Premiership form:.

Hibernian are without right-back options Felix Passlack and Kanayochukwu Megwa due to respective hamstring and thigh problems, while centre-back Rocky Bushiri remains sidelined with an Achilles injury.

With that in mind, Alex Williams could start on the right of a four-man defence featuring Jason Kerr, Marko Ivezic and Jack Iredale in front of goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger.

At the opposite end of the pitch, striker Nathan Lowe is out injured, so 20-year-old Owen Elding is likely to operate up top, supported by Josh Mulligan and Martin Boyle from out wide.

As for Dundee Utd, they are missing right-sided attacker Neil Farrugia due to a groin injury, though Jesse Randall should be on hand to start as part of a trio alongside Dylan Tait and Daniel Bennie behind Zachary Sapsford.

Left-back Will ferry is also dealing with a muscle injury, while midfielder Emmanuel Agyei is recovering from a knee matter.

In their absence, Kevin Ciubotaru looks set to start on the left side of the visiting defence, with Lyall Cameron and Zidane Iqbal forming Goodwin's double pivot.

Hibernian possible starting lineup:.

Sallinger; Williams, Kerr, Ivezic, Iredale; Chaiwa, Newell; Mulligan, McGrath, Boyle; Elding.

Dundee United possible starting lineup:.

Walton; Rawlins, Esselink, Forbes, Ciubotaru; Cameron, Iqbal; Randall, Tait, Bennie; Sapsford.

Hibernian have struggled this term and are sat near the bottom of the table, but their results picked up prior to the international break, and they will be motivated to continue their burgeoning resurgence under Reedijk.

Dundee Utd have proven resilient so far and their unbeaten streak is unlikely to be broken at Easter Road, though they could fall short of winning on Saturday.

By Lewis Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 02:54, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:03.

Liverpool's Premier League campaign resumes at Anfield on Sunday, when they take on fierce rivals Manchester United.

The hosts come into the clash in fourth place with 18 points after 10 matchweeks, whereas United are in 18th place with just eight points.

Andoni Iraola will know the importance of winning at Anfield considering he has already lost against Manchester City and Arsenal, and he cannot afford a loss against the Red Devils at their lowest moment.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their Premier League fixture against Man United.

© Imago / David Rawcliffe, Propaganda Photo.

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United).

Ryan Gravenberch was left on the bench against Arsenal on November 1, and he was left out of the squad that faced Fenerbahce three days later.

Iraola confirmed that he was dealing with a fracture in his foot, though despite missing his side's win against Crystal Palace before the November international break, he could make his return against Man United.

© Iconsport / Marty Jean-Louis/Sipa USA.

Sources indicate that possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United).

Speedster Jeremie Frimpong was brought on at half time against Brentford on October 17 but had to be replaced just seven minutes later with a hamstring injury.

According to recent reports, the right-back is set to be sidelined until after the international break, and Iraola stated on October 19, "It’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it's going to be difficult to have him.".

Frimpong did not return before the break, but he could return to the squad against Man United.

According to recent reports, possible return date: December 26 (vs. Hull City).

Striker Hugo Ekitike has been out of action since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April, and is going through rehabilitation following surgery on the tear.

The Frenchman is unlikely to take to the pitch for some weeks, but has been included in Liverpool's squad for the Champions League league-phase, and could return during the festive period.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Nineteen-year-old centre-back Giovanni Leoni is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury on his debut in September 2025.

In a recent development, speaking on October 15, Iraola revealed that the defender has faced a setback, saying, "It’s taking more time than we wanted. The proposal was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next [one].".

The defender has since returned to parts of team training, though he is far behind the rest of the squad.

Industry observers note that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Right-back Conor Bradley has been unavailable since picking up a major knee injury against Arsenal in January, though he is planning a return this autumn.

The academy graduate has yet to join team training, but is making progress in his rehabilitation and started doing ball work earlier this month.

Much like Leoni, the right-back has returned to parts of team training, but Liverpool are set to take a cautious approach to his fitness.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

Recent findings suggest that the owner wants Tresoldi and is ready to sit at the table himself, while Nicolò remains ready to serve him a winning first pass. Milan want him in January, but if that weren’t possible, they would leave the discussion open for the summer.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER and LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 02:49 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 16:51 EST, 18 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino has issued a rallying cry to Manchester United supporters, promising that this is going to be a 'special season' despite their dismal start which sees them 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 games.

The latest Red Devils head coach landed in Manchester on Wednesday morning, hopping straight off a private jet to meet his new players, hours after leading the USA in his final game as their boss.

And during a busy first day among his fresh surroundings, the Argentine sent a direct message to the club's fanbase as he preached for unity.

'Hi Reds, here's it's Mauricio Pochettino,' he stated via a video posted on United's X account at 7.15pm on Wednesday evening.

Recent findings suggest that 'I am looking forward to meeting you guys. I hear so many good things about you.

'I hope we bring all the happiness working together and connecting together.

A message from Mauricio 💬❤️🤳 #ShotOnSnapdragon pic.twitter.com/2lBLkMaGY6.

Mauricio Pochettino addressed Manchester United fans directly on Wednesday evening after starting work officially as their new head coach.

The newly introduced Red Devils head coach has promised a 'special season' in a direct message to fans.

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday.

'This is going to be a special season to support and to make our players to fight on the field and to get the results that we deserve.'.

It has been revealed that in a second message in his native Spanish, Pochettino expanded further: 'This message is about being united, like the name Manchester United. We all need to work together.

'I hope to bring the happy moments that this club deserves and create the unity that every team needs so that the players can be at their best on the pitch.'.

Those messages came less than eight hours after arriving in England. He landed in Manchester at 11.32am on Wednesday and immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff.

Speaking to the club's media channels earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino mentioned: 'Thank you so much, I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work.'.

The club then officially welcomed the newly introduced manager on their website, writing: 'Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian.

Recent findings suggest that 'Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA. Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.'.

Pochettino had made a promise to end Man City's dominance as United manager in his last interview as United States national team coach on Tuesday evening.

He took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet chartered by the club after his final match on American soil, which saw the US beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati.

But before becoming airborne, Pochettino had time for a final statement Stateside, after being taunted that 'Manchester is blue, and will always be blue' by one of his interviewers.

Earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino made his way to Carrington straight after landing in Manchester, meeting players and staff and taking a tour.

The Argentine took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet last night and landed at 11.32am.

The manager shared a picture from his journey as he prepared to touch down at the airport (Source: Instagram/Mauricio Pochettino).

'No way,' he shook his head. 'You will see.'.

'Give me time. Give me time and then that - that's going to change.'.

Pochettino also shared a poignant farewell message to his US set-up, days after breaking down in tears in a press conference ahead of his penultimate time in charge.

Man United fans may also have been pleased to read of Pochettino's latest-found love of John Denver's song Country Roads in his goodbye message, a song which is played before kick-off at Old Trafford.

'It is never easy to say goodbye, especially after everything we experienced together.' Pochettino captioned a carousel of photos of his time in the role. 'I always wanted the opportunity to coach in the USA, and I was very happy to have this chance with the national team. Two incredible years, with so many great moments and experiences that will stay with me always.

'From the challenges we faced at the Gold Cup to the excitement of the USA hosting the World Cup, and now finishing our time by reaching the semi-finals of the Nations League, I am proud of what we achieved.

Recent findings suggest that 'When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team. Not everything in football can be measured by results, and I believe we have helped build something important for the future of soccer in this country.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

'This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. I have discovered a wonderful country, made upcoming friends and enjoyed so many of the traditions. Every time I hear Country Roads, I will forever think of all of you with a smile.

'Thank you to the players, staff, everyone at (the US national team) and all the supporters. Especially to those who believed in us and gave us this opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that 'Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

'I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves. Thank you USA.'.

Pochettino had previously explained his emotions as stemming from how difficult the decision had been to leave the national team and re-start at Old Trafford.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he stated on Friday. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

In a recent development, ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Man United first made contact with Pochettino following their breathless 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in their last match before the international break.

The Man United hierarchy had previously given former head coach Michael Carrick a stay of execution amid a worrying start to the season, but as they prepared to head into the two-week pause in the relegation zone, the board became keen to make a change.

An agonising wait for Carrick followed, with the club legend taking training for multiple sessions at the start of the week as his future was openly mulled by executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

After the duo returned from Monaco, where they had flown to speak to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe about Carrick's future, the 45-year-old was finally dispatched last Thursday morning.

In their statement regarding Pochettino's arrival on Wednesday, United also confirmed the exits of Carrick and Co, writing: 'The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

'We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future.'.

Pochettino's United States farewell match went off in pitch-perfect style, which allowed thoughts to quickly move to the next task at hand after the final whistle.

Christian Pulisic helped make sure that Pochettino's reign in charge ended on a high note.

The manager will now focus his attentions on getting Man United out of the relegation zone.

'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino remarked after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'.

Travelling with Pochettino were outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott, while his assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

Man United paid a staggering £10million to cleave Pochettino and his staff away from the United States, after the head coach signed a newly introduced contract with the national team in the wake of this summer's World Cup.

Sources indicate that the quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

Recent findings suggest that 'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'.

According to recent reports, sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

According to recent reports, on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

According to recent reports, "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Recent findings suggest that neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It has been revealed that it begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the blueprint to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

Industry observers note that that still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

In a recent development, the goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

Industry observers note that "A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

According to recent reports, fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their fresh head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

In a recent development, united’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Industry observers note that but, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

According to recent reports, might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Recent findings suggest that "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

In a recent development, I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

Recent findings suggest that I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

In a recent development, we wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a massive team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so important for us.

There were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

In the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

Industry observers note that I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

It has been revealed that it was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

It was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

According to recent reports, the defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

According to recent reports, fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

It has been revealed that united almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

According to recent reports, united’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

The game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

In a recent development, cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

In a recent development, mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

This stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

It has been revealed that fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

Bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa.

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces.

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

Fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

The interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

Industry observers note that fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

Bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

Industry observers note that A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

United have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

Industry observers note that fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

It has been revealed that promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

According to recent reports, if Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Recent findings suggest that michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia.

Industry observers note that subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe.

Recent findings suggest that here's how The Fulham shape up. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/0IxS0J3ldf.

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊.

In a recent development, the script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a significant impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager remarked.

Industry observers note that “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty substantial one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

Sources indicate that “But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he mentioned it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

Sources indicate that the mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

According to recent reports, fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

Falkirk vs St Johnstone - prediction, team news, lineups

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 03:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 05:20.
  • Fighting for a spot in the top half of the Scottish Premiership, promoted St Johnstone will lock horns with in-form Falkirk at Falkirk Stadium on Saturday.
  • The Bairns are eyeing a sixth win on the bounce, while the Saints could go four games unbeaten this weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 03:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 05:20.

Fighting for a spot in the top half of the Scottish Premiership, promoted St Johnstone will lock horns with in-form Falkirk at Falkirk Stadium on Saturday.

The Bairns are eyeing a sixth win on the bounce, while the Saints could go four games unbeaten this weekend.

John McGlynn's Falkirk are the form team in the Scottish top flight over the past five games, and they will be confident of earning maximum points yet again on home turf.

The latest in their string of triumphs was a 5-2 demolition of last term's runners-up Hearts at Tynecastle Park, where the Bairns raced into a 4-0 lead by the half-time interval.

Bolstering the magnitude of McGlynn's side's feat further is the fact that thrashing followed a 2-0 win against Celtic, which itself marked a third consecutive clean sheet.

All in all, taking 15 points from the last 15 on offer has put Falkirk third in the Scottish Premiership, though their 21-point tally leaves them six behind second-placed Rangers and 10 short of top-of-the-table Celtic.

On the other hand, the Bairns are now four points clear of their seventh-placed opponents, and boasting the second-best defensive record in the division, McGlynn will be optimistic about his team's chances of seeing extending that advantage.

Meanwhile, St Johnstone earned promotion to the top flight by winning the Scottish Championship last term, and while plenty of sides have struggled with the step up in the past, Simo Valakari's men are in a strong position.

The Saints are currently seventh with 17 points after 13 games, level with sixth-placed Dundee United and fifth-placed Dundee.

Prior to the international break, Valakari's side downed the Dee 2-1, taking an early lead via Josh Campbell before Kai Fotheringham won the clash roughly 20 minutes from time.

That victory ended a four-game run without a win, though St Johnstone had only tasted defeat once during that stretch, and arrive with just a single loss from their last seven outings overall.

The visitors will be the underdogs on Saturday, but buoyed by their resilience - as well as having scored more goals (17) than any other team in the bottom half - they are sure to fight for the chance to climb into the top six.

Falkirk Scottish Premiership form:.

St Johnstone Scottish Premiership form:.

Falkirk will be without injured full-backs Ryan Strain and Leon McCann, though Jack McMillan and Scott Tanser should be on hand to start either side of centre-halves Lewis Neilson and Liam Henderson.

At the opposite end of the pitch, right wingers Aodhan Doherty and Joseph Gardner are dealing with respective foot and thigh injuries, while the left-sided Ethan Laidlaw and attacking midfielder Aidan Nesbitt have ankle concerns to contend with.

In their absence, Jacob Murrell looks set to start up top, supported by Ethan Ross, Finley Barbrook and Owen Eames.

As for St Johnstone, they have a generally fit squad, with centre-back Bozo Mikulic reportedly available after breaking his nose against Dundee just 14 minutes into his return from 20 months out with an ACL injury and a slew of problems in the aftermath.

Elsewhere, Joel Cotterill could operate alongside Jason Holt in the centre of the park, flanked by wing-backs Liam Smith and Josh Campbell.

Falkirk possible starting lineup:.

Bain; McMillan, Neilson, Henderson, Tanser; Spencer, Melniks; Ross, Barbrook, Eames; Murrell.

St Johnstone possible starting lineup:.

Steward; Diabate, Finlayson, Alic; Smith, Cotterill, Holt, Campbell; Steven, Schmidt, Fotheringham.

In the midst of more than just a purple patch, Falkirk have been immense of late, hammering Hearts, beating Celtic and maintaining a strong defensive record.

St Johnstone have proven their own resilience since making the step back up to the Premiership, but they will be hard-pressed to hold out against the division's form team.

#37959. Latest Update: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 64m • 📚 Deep Dive (12787 w)
📖 Baca
